<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:existenceQOTbary_intro} Let $[N]$ be an index set of $N\in\mathbb N$ elements and
$\boldsymbol{\alpha}:=(\alpha_s)_{s\in[N]}$ be positive real numbers satisfying
$\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s = 1$. Let 
$\mathcal{H}_0$ and $(\mathcal{H}_s)_{s\in[N]}$ be separable Hilbert spaces, and
$\boldsymbol{\sigma}:=(\sigma_s)_{s\in[N]}$ with $\sigma_s\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_s)$ be a family of quantum states. 

Let $\mathbf{C}:=(C_s)_{s\in[N]}$ be a family of nonnegative self-adjoint cost operators $C_s\in\mathcal{L}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)$. Assume that there exists $s_0\in[N]$ such that one of the following conditions holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $C_{s_0}$ has compact resolvent on
$\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_{s_0}$;

\item[(ii)] $C_{s_0}$ is a quadrature-generated cost, the associated one-body square-sum $H_0^{(s_0)}$ on $\mathcal{H}_0$ has compact resolvent, and the one-body square-sum $H^{(s_0)}$ on
$\mathcal{H}_{s_0}$ satisfies $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\bigl(H^{(s_0)}\sigma_{s_0}\bigr)<+\infty$.
\end{itemize}

Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathbf E=(E_1,\ldots,E_k)\in[0,+\infty)^k$ and $\mathbf A:=(A_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]}$, where
$A_\ell\in\mathcal{L}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H}_0)$ for every $\ell\in[k]$. Assume that the constrained barycentric state set $\mathcal{S}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\mathcal{H}_0)$, defined in \eqref{eq:constrain}, is nonempty and that there exists $\rho_0\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\mathcal{H}_0)$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exas}
\sum_{s=1}^{N}\alpha_s\,\operatorname{QOT}\!\big(\rho_0,\sigma_s\mid C_s\big)<+\infty.
\end{equation}
Then the QOT barycenter problem~\eqref{intro:QOT-barycenter} admits a barycenter.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:energy-constrained-barycenter-duality}
Under the same hypotheses as in Theorem~\ref{thm:existenceQOTbary_intro}, the following duality formula holds for the QOT barycenter problem~\eqref{intro:QOT-barycenter}:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:energy-constrained-duality-barycenter}
\mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})
=
\sup
\left\{
\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
-
\sum_{\ell\in[k]}\eta_\ell E_\ell
:
((U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]},(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]})
\in
\mathsf{Pot}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\right\}, 
\end{equation}
where 
$\mathsf{Pot}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)$
is the set of admissible energy-constrained potentials defined by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pot}
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{Pot}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
:=
\Bigl\{ &((U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]},(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]})
:
\, U_s\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0),\,
V_s\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_s),\, U_s\oplus V_s\le C_s,
\\
&
\text{there exist }
U_s^{(\ell)}\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0) 
\text{ such that }
U_s=\sum_{\ell=1}^k U_s^{(\ell)}\, \text{for all }
s\in[N], \,
\\
&
-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}
\le
\eta_\ell A_\ell \text{ and }\eta_\ell\ge0\, \text{for all } \ell\in[k]  \, 
\Bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- coro-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:unconstrained-barycenter-duality}
Assume the cost assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:existenceQOTbary_intro} and assume that
there exists \(\rho_0\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0)\) such that $\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s \operatorname{QOT}(\rho_0,\sigma_s\mid C_s)<+\infty$. Then we have the following dual formula for \eqref{eq:unconstrained-barycenter-primal}:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:unconstrained-barycenter-duality}
\mathcal{B}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}_0(\boldsymbol{\sigma})
=
\sup
\left\{
\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
:
(U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]}
\in
\mathsf{Pot}_0^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\right\},
\end{equation}
where the admissible potential set is
\[
\mathsf{Pot}_0^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}(\boldsymbol\sigma)
:=
\left\{
(U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]}:
\begin{array}{l}
U_s\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0),\quad V_s\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_s),
\\[1mm]
\displaystyle \sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s U_s=0, \quad U_s\oplus V_s\le C_s,\quad s\in[N]
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
<!-- end coro-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:finitesecondemomentrho}
Assume the cost assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:existenceQOTbary_intro} in the
unconstrained case, and assume in addition that every \(C_s\) is quadrature-generated. Let \(H^{(s)}_0\) and \(H^{(s)}\) be the one-body square-sums associated with $C_s$ as in~\eqref{intro:eq:one-body-H}. Assume, in addition, that $\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(H^{(s)}\sigma_s\bigr)<+\infty$ for all $s\in[N]$. Let $\overline{\rho}\in
\mathrm{Bar}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}_0(\boldsymbol\sigma)$ be a QOT barycenter. If 
\[
M:=\inf_{\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0)}\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\Big(\rho H_0^{(s)}\Big) < \infty,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\Big(\overline{\rho} H_0^{(s)}\Big)
 \le \frac83M+\frac{20}{3}\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\sigma_s H^{(s)})<+\infty.
\end{equation}

Consequently, the minimum in~\eqref{eq:unconstrained-barycenter-primal}
is unchanged if the barycentric search space is restricted to $
\bigcap_{s=1}^N
\left\{
\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0):
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl(H_0^{(s)}\rho\bigr)<+\infty
\right\}$.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:gaussian-barycenter-intro}
For each $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, consider the $2$-QW barycenter problem 
\eqref{eq:tau-barycenter-intro} with Gaussian inputs
$\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^G$:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:gaussianqw}
\min_{\hat\rho\in\mathcal{S}(L_2(\mathbb R^m))}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\,\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s^G).
\end{equation}
Then \eqref{eq:gaussianqw} admits a Gaussian barycenter. Every Gaussian
barycenter has mean
\[
\overline{\mathbf m}
=
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\mathbf m_s.
\]
Define the Gaussian barycenter covariance problem by
\begin{equation}
\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}
:=
\min_{\substack{
\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_m^{\mathrm Q},\\
A_s\in\mathrm{Corr}_{\tau}(\Sigma,\Sigma_s),\ s\in[N]}}
\left\{
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma)
+
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_s)-2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)\bigr)
\right\}.
\label{eq:qw2cov}
\end{equation}
The covariance matrix of every Gaussian barycenter is the first
component of an optimizer of \eqref{eq:qw2cov}. Conversely, every
optimizer of \eqref{eq:qw2cov}, together with the mean
$\overline{\mathbf m}$, determines a Gaussian barycenter. Here
$\tau=+1$ gives the quantum-state formulation and $\tau=-1$ the
quantum-channel formulation.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:faithful-global-uniqueness-intro}
Under the assumptions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian-barycenter-intro}, suppose that at least one
input Gaussian state is faithful, that is, for some $s_0\in[N]$,
\[
\Sigma_{s_0}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\succ0.
\]
Then, for each $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, the $2$-QW barycenter problem
\eqref{eq:gaussianqw} for the Gaussian inputs
$\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^G$ admits a unique barycenter among all
quantum states. This barycenter is Gaussian; its mean and covariance
are characterized by
Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian-barycenter-intro}.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:gaussian-semiclassical-intro}
For sufficiently small $\hbar>0$, let
$\hat\sigma_s^\hbar$ be the Gaussian state with mean
$\mathbf m_s$ and covariance $\Sigma_s$, $s\in[N]$.
For each $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, consider the corresponding $2$-QW
barycenter problem
$$
\min_{\hat\rho\in\mathcal{S}(L_2(\mathbb R^m))}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\,
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s^\hbar).
$$
By Theorem~\ref{thm:faithful-global-uniqueness-intro}, its barycenter
$\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^\hbar$ is uniquely defined and Gaussian,
with mean $\overline{\mathbf m}$. Writing its covariance as
$\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)$, one has 
$\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)
\rightarrow
\overline\Sigma$ as $\hbar\to0^+$.


Consequently, for both the quantum-state and quantum-channel formulations, the Wigner distributions
$\mathbb W_{\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^\hbar}(\mathbf z)\,d\mathbf z$ converge weakly to
$\mathcal N(\overline{\mathbf m},\overline\Sigma)$, the classical
$2$-Wasserstein barycenter of $\{\mathcal N(\mathbf m_s,\Sigma_s)\}_{s\in[N]}$ with weights $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:thermal-barycenter-intro}
For each $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, the $2$-QW barycenter problem
\begin{equation}\label{eq:thermalqw}
\min_{\hat\rho\in\mathcal{S}(L_2(\mathbb R^m))}
\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s\,\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s^{\mathrm{th}})
\end{equation}
admits a unique barycenter
$\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau$. It is a displaced isotropic thermal
state with mean $\overline{\mathbf m}=\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\mathbf m_s$ and covariance
$\overline\Sigma_\tau=\overline w_\tau\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$.

For the quantum-state formulation,
\[
\overline w_{+1}
=
\left(
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\sqrt{w_s-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right)^2
+
\frac{\hbar}{2}.
\]
For the quantum-channel formulation,
\[
\{\overline w_{-1}\}
=
\operatorname{argmin}_{w\geq\hbar/2}
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{w_s<w}
\alpha_s
\left[
\sqrt{w+\frac{\hbar}{2}}
-
\sqrt{w_s-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2\\
&\quad+
\sum_{w_s\geq w}
\alpha_s
\left[
\sqrt{w_s+\frac{\hbar}{2}}
-
\sqrt{w-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2
\end{aligned}
\right\}.
\]
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- deff-1: body_md -->
\label{def:compact-resolvent}
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable Hilbert space, and let $H\in\mathcal{L}_S(\mathcal{H})$ be a self-adjoint
operator on $\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathrm{spec}(H)$ be the spectrum of $H$.
The resolvent set of $H$ is then $\mathrm{res}(H):=\mathbb C\setminus\mathrm{spec}(H)$. For $z\in\mathrm{res}(H)$, the resolvent of $H$ at $z$ is the bounded operator
\[
    R_z(H):=(H-z\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}})^{-1}.
\]
We say that $H$ has compact resolvent if $R_z(H)\in\mathcal{K}(\mathcal{H})$ is compact for some,
equivalently for every, $z\in\mathrm{res}(H)$.
<!-- end deff-1 -->
<!-- deff-2: body_md -->
\label{def:spectral-integral-traceclass}
Let $A\in\mathcal{L}_S(\mathcal{H})$ be self-adjoint and let $\rho\in\mathcal{T}^{(1)}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H})$.
We define the spectral integral of $A$ against $\rho$ by
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A\rho)
\ :=\
\int_{\mathbb R} \lambda\, d\mu_\rho^A(\lambda)
\ \in\ [-\infty,+\infty],
\]
whenever the integral is well-defined in the extended sense, i.e.\ whenever at
least one of the positive/negative parts is finite:
\[
\int_{\mathbb R} \lambda^+\, d\mu_\rho^A(\lambda)<+\infty
\quad \text{or}\quad
\int_{\mathbb R} \lambda^-\, d\mu_\rho^A(\lambda)<+\infty,
\]
where $\lambda^\pm:=\max\{\pm\lambda,0\}$.
<!-- end deff-2 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:spectral-trunc-positive}
Let $A\in\mathcal{L}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H})$ be self-adjoint and positive semidefinite, and let
$\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$.
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, define the bounded spectral truncations
\[
A^{(n)}
:=
\int_{[0,n]} \lambda\, dE^A(\lambda)
\ \in\ \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}).
\]
Then $0\le A^{(n)}\le A^{(n+1)}\le A$, and
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A\rho)
=
\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\big(\,A^{(n)}\rho\big)
=
\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\big(\,A^{(n)}\rho\big)
\ \in\ [0,+\infty],
\]
with the convention that the right-hand side may be $+\infty$.
Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A\rho )
=
\sup\Bigl\{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(B\rho ):\ B\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}),\ 0\le B\le A\Bigr\}.
\]
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By construction, $\mu_\rho^A$ is a finite positive measure on $\mathbb R$ and
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A\rho )
=
\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\, d\mu_\rho^A(\lambda)
=
\int_{[0,\infty)}\lambda\, d\mu_\rho^A(\lambda)\in[0,+\infty].
\]
Moreover, $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\big(\,A^{(n)}\rho\big)
=
\int_{[0,n]} \lambda\, d\mu_\rho^A(\lambda)$, hence $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}( A^{(n)}\rho)\uparrow \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A\rho)$ by monotone convergence for
nonnegative functions.
Finally, for any $B\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H})$ with $0\le B\le A$, one has
$\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(B\rho)\le \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A\rho)$, and taking $B=A^{(n)}$ yields the supremum
representation.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- deff-3: body_md -->
\label{def:partialtrace}
Let $\mathcal{H}_1,\mathcal{H}_2$ be separable Hilbert spaces and $T\in\mathcal{T}^{(1)}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)$.
The partial traces $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}(T)\in\mathcal{T}^{(1)}(\mathcal{H}_1)$ and
$\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}(T)\in\mathcal{T}^{(1)}(\mathcal{H}_2)$ are the unique trace-class operators such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:partialtrace}
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl(B_1\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}(T)\bigr)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl((B_1\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2})\,T\bigr),
\qquad
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl(B_2\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}(T)\bigr)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl((\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}\otimes B_2)\,T\bigr),
\end{equation}
for all $B_1\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_1)$ and $B_2\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_2)$.
<!-- end deff-3 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:pt-continuity}
For $T\in\mathcal{T}^{(1)}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)$ one has
$\|\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}(T)\|_1\le \|T\|_1$ and $\|\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}(T)\|_1\le \|T\|_1$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We prove the first inequality. By duality of $\mathcal{T}^{(1)}(\mathcal{H}_1)$ and $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_1)$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}(T)\|_1
&=\sup_{\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 1}
\big|\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\big(A\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}(T)\big)\big|\\
&=\sup_{\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 1}
\big|\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\big((A\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2})T\big)\big|\\
&\le \sup_{\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le 1}|\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(BT)|=\|T\|_1.
\end{aligned}
\]
The second inequality is analogous.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:partialtrace-unbounded}
Let $A\in\mathcal{L}_S(\mathcal{H}_1)$ and $\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)$. Then $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(A(\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\pi)\right)$ is well defined if and only if $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left((A\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2})\pi\right)$ is well defined, and in this case 
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(A(\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\pi)\right)=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left((A\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2})\pi\right).
\]
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By the spectral calculus, $E^{A\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}}(B)=E^A(B)\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}$ for every Borel set $B\subset\mathbb R$. Hence, by the defining property of
the partial trace,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_{\pi}^{A\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}}(B)=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left[
E^{A\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}}(B)\pi
\right]=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left[
(E^A(B)\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2})\pi
\right]=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left[E^A(B)
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\pi
\right]
=
\mu_{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\pi}^{A}(B).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the two scalar spectral measures coincide. Therefore their
positive and negative spectral integrals are finite simultaneously,
and, whenever the corresponding extended expectations are well defined,
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(A\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\pi\right)
=
\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu_{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\pi}^{A}(\lambda)
=
\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,
d\mu_{\pi}^{A\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}}(\lambda)
=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left((A\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2})\pi\right).
\]
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- deff-4: body_md -->
\label{def:quantumcouplings}
Let $\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1)$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_2)$.
A \emph{coupling} of $(\rho,\sigma)$ is a state $\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)$ such that $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}(\pi)=\rho$ and $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}(\pi)=\sigma$. We denote the set of all such couplings by
\begin{equation}\label{def:quantumcoupling}
\Gamma(\rho,\sigma):=\bigl\{\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2):\ \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\pi=\rho,\ \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}\pi=\sigma\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end deff-4 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:quadratic-hamiltonian-esa}
Let \(\Theta\in\mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)\) be a nondegenerate skew-symmetric matrix, $W:\mathbb R^{2m}\to\mathcal U(\mathcal H)$ be a regular \(\Theta\)-Weyl system on a Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and \(\mathbf{R}=(R_1,\ldots,R_{2m})\) be its canonical
generators.

Let \(G\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)\) be real symmetric, \(\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^{2m}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R\).
Define, on the common smooth domain \(\mathcal H_R^\infty\),
\[
  H_{G,\mathbf{a},c}^{(0)}
  :=
  \frac12\sum_{j,k=1}^{2m}G_{jk}R_jR_k
  +\sum_{j=1}^{2m}a_jR_j
  +c\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{H}=\frac12\mathbf{R}^\top G\mathbf{R}+\mathbf{a}^\top\mathbf{R}
  +c\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{H}.
\]
Then \(H_{G,\mathbf{a},c}^{(0)}\) is a well-defined symmetric operator on
\(\mathcal H_R^\infty\) and is essentially self-adjoint on
\(\mathcal H_R^\infty\).
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:quadratic-hamiltonian-closure-convention} In what follows, whenever a Hamiltonian can be written as \[ H_{G,\mathbf{a},c} = \frac12\sum_{j,k=1}^{2m}G_{jk}R_jR_k +\sum_{j=1}^{2m}a_jR_j +c\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{H}, \] it is understood as the unique self-adjoint extension, equivalently the closure, of the operator \(H_{G,\mathbf{a},c}^{(0)}\) initially defined on \(\mathcal H_R^\infty\). 

In particular, all quadrature-generated costs and one-body square-sums defined in Section~\ref{intro:statementofresults} are understood in this closure sense. Thus the operators are well-defined self-adjoint operators.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{theo:stone}
Let \(\Theta\in\mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)\) be a nondegenerate skew-symmetric matrix, $W:\mathbb R^{2m}\to\mathcal U(\mathcal H)$ be a regular \(\Theta\)-Weyl system on a Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and \(\mathbf{R}=(R_1,\ldots,R_{2m})\) be its canonical generators as defined above. Choose \(L\in \mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)\) such that
\[
L^\top(\hbar\Omega_m)L=\Theta.
\]
Then there exist a Hilbert space \(\mathcal K\) and a unitary $U:L_2(\mathbb R^m)\otimes\mathcal K\to\mathcal H$ such that
\[
U^\dagger W(\xi)U
=
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(L\xi)\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{K}}=e^{i\xi^\top L^\top\hat{\mathbf R}}\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{K}},\quad
U^\dagger R(\xi)U
=(\xi^\top L^\top\hat{\mathbf R})\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal K}.
\]
The representation is irreducible if and only if \(\mathcal K=\mathbb C\).
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:stone-reference}
Theorem~\ref{theo:stone} is the finite-dimensional Stone--von Neumann theorem with
multiplicity, written in coordinates adapted to the skew-symmetric matrix \(\Theta\). The
linear change of variables reduces the \(\Theta\)-Weyl relations to the standard
\((\hbar\Omega_m)\)-Weyl relations. We refer to
\cite[Props.~15--16, Thm.~19, Cor.~20]{AraiGCCR} for generalized CCR systems and to
\cite[Thm.~4]{DerezinskiCCR} for the regular finite-dimensional CCR Stone--von Neumann
theorem with multiplicity.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- coro-2: body_md -->
\label{coro:nelson-square-compact-resolvent}
Let \(\Theta\in\mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)\) be a nondegenerate skew-symmetric matrix, $W:\mathbb R^{2m}\to\mathcal U(\mathcal H)$ be an irreducible regular \(\Theta\)-Weyl system on a Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), and \(\mathbf{R}=(R_1,\ldots,R_{2m})\) be its canonical generators. Let $\mathsf H_{\mathbf R}
  :=\sum_{j=1}^{2m}R_j^2$ be the one-body square-sum on $\mathcal{H}$. Then \(\mathsf H_{\mathbf R}\in\mathcal{L}_S(\mathcal{H})\) is a nonnegative self-adjoint operator
with compact resolvent.
<!-- end coro-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{theo:stone} and irreducibility, the multiplicity space is
\(\mathbb C\). Hence \(\mathsf H_{\mathbf R}\) is unitarily equivalent to the operator
\[
  \sum_{j=1}^{2m}
  \bigl((L^\top\hat{\mathbf R})_j\bigr)^2
  =
  \hat{\mathbf R}^\top LL^\top\hat{\mathbf R},
\]
where \(L\in \mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)\) satisfies
\(L^\top(\hbar\Omega_m)L=\Theta\). Since \(LL^\top\) is positive
definite, this is an elliptic positive quadratic Hamiltonian in the standard canonical variables. By the standard spectral theory of positive quadratic Hamiltonians, it has
discrete spectrum with finite multiplicities, equivalently compact resolvent;
see \cite[Sec.~26]{Shubin2001}. Hence \(\mathsf H_{\mathbf R}\) has compact
resolvent.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:tau-standard-CCR-identification}
We have
\begin{equation}
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{L_2(\mathbb R^m)}\otimes J_{\tau,m}\bigr)^\dagger
\hat{\mathbf R}_{+1}
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{L_2(\mathbb R^m)}\otimes J_{\tau,m}\bigr)
=
(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m})
\hat{\mathbf R}_\tau,
\label{eq:tau-standard-canonical-identification}
\end{equation}
where the left unitary conjugation is understood
componentwise, while the right real matrices act on its phase-space index. In particular,
\begin{equation}
(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m})
\bigl(
\Omega_m\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_m)
\bigr)
(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m})^\top
=
\Omega_{2m}.
\label{eq:tau-standard-symplectic-identification}
\end{equation}
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Equation~\eqref{eq:tau-standard-canonical-identification} follows
componentwise from the definition of $J_{\tau,m}$ and the identities
for $\hat Q_j^\top$ and $\hat P_j^\top$ above. Moreover,
$F_{\tau,m}(\tau\Omega_m)F_{\tau,m}^\top=\Omega_m$, which gives
\eqref{eq:tau-standard-symplectic-identification}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:compact1}
Let $\mathcal{H}_0,\mathcal{H}$ be separable Hilbert spaces, let
$\sigma\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$, and let $c\ge0$. Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item
Let $C\in\mathcal{L}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H})$ have compact resolvent. Then
\[
\mathcal{A}(\sigma,c)
:=
\Bigl\{
\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}):
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi=\sigma,\ 
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C\pi)\le c
\Bigr\}
\]
is compact in the trace-norm topology.

\item
Let $H\in\mathcal{L}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H}_0)$ have compact resolvent. Then
\[
\mathcal{A}_H(\sigma,c)
:=
\Bigl\{
\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}):
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi=\sigma,\ 
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl(H\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}}\pi\bigr)\le c
\Bigr\}
\]
is compact in the trace-norm topology.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
For~(i), let $(\pi_n)_n\subset\mathcal{A}(\sigma,c)$. Since $C$ has compact
resolvent and $\sup_n\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C\pi_n)\le c$, Lemma~\ref{lemma:boundedHcompact} yields a subsequence
$(\pi_{n_k})_k$ and a state
$\widetilde\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H})$ such that $\pi_{n_k}\rightarrow\widetilde\pi$ in trace norm and $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C\widetilde\pi)\le c$. By the trace-norm continuity of the partial trace,
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\widetilde\pi
=
\lim_{k\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi_{n_k}
=
\sigma.
\]
Hence $\widetilde\pi\in\mathcal{A}(\sigma,c)$, proving that
$\mathcal{A}(\sigma,c)$ is compact.

For~(ii), let $(\pi_n)_n\subset\mathcal{A}_H(\sigma,c)$. The bound $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}}\pi_n)\le c$ and Lemma~\ref{lemma:boundedHcompact} yield a subsequence
$(\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}}\pi_{n_k})_k$ and a state $\widetilde\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0)$ such that $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}}\pi_{n_k}\rightarrow\widetilde\rho$ in trace norm. Since $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi_{n_k}=\sigma$ for every $k$, Theorem~\ref{theo:compact} yields a further subsequence,
which we do not relabel, and a state
$\widetilde\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H})$ such that $\pi_{n_k}\rightarrow\widetilde\pi$ in trace norm, with
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\widetilde\pi=\sigma,
\qquad
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}}\widetilde\pi=\widetilde\rho.
\]
Finally, by the lower semicontinuity of
$\rho\mapsto\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho)$,
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\widetilde\rho)
\le
\liminf_{k\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}}\pi_{n_k})
\le c.
\]
Hence $\widetilde\pi\in\mathcal{A}_H(\sigma,c)$, proving that
$\mathcal{A}_H(\sigma,c)$ is compact.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- coro-3: body_md -->
\label{coro:compactc}
Let $S$ be a finite index set.
Assume that $S$ is partitioned as $S=S_{\mathrm{I}}\sqcup S_{\mathrm{F}}$. Let $\mathcal{H}_0$ and $\mathcal{H}_s$ for all $s\in S$ be separable Hilbert spaces. For each $s\in S_{\mathrm{I}}$, let $C_s\in\mathcal{L}_\geq(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)$ be a cost operator with compact resolvent.
For each $s\in S_{\mathrm{F}}$, let $H_s\in\mathcal{L}_\geq(\mathcal{H}_0)$ be a nonnegative operator with compact resolvent.

For each $s\in S$, let $\sigma_s\in \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_s)$ and $c_s\in\mathbb R_+$.
Define the feasible set
\[
\mathcal{A}_s :=
\begin{cases}
\bigl\{\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s):\ \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi=\sigma_s,\ \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_s\pi)\le c_s\bigr\},
& s\in S_{\mathrm{I}},\\[1mm]
\bigl\{\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s):\ \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi=\sigma_s,\ \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl(H_s\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi\bigr)\le c_s\bigr\},
& s\in S_{\mathrm{F}}.
\end{cases}
\]
Finally, set
\[
\mathcal{A} :=
\Bigl\{(\pi_s)_{s\in S}\in\prod_{s\in S}\mathcal{A}_s:\ \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi_s=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_{s'}}\pi_{s'}\ \text{for all } s,s'\in S\Bigr\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal{A}$ is compact in the norm $\|(\,T_s\,)_{s\in S}\|:=\sum_{s\in S}\|T_s\|_1$.
<!-- end coro-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
For each $s\in S_{\mathrm I}$, the set $\mathcal{A}_s$ is compact by
Proposition~\ref{prop:compact1}(i), whereas for each
$s\in S_{\mathrm F}$ it is compact by
Proposition~\ref{prop:compact1}(ii). Since $S$ is finite, the product $\prod_{s\in S}\mathcal{A}_s$ is compact for the product topology,
and the norm $\sum_{s\in S}\|\cdot\|_1$ induces an equivalent metrization. The constraint $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi_s=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_{s'}}\pi_{s'}$ for all $s,s'\in S$ defines a closed subset of the product,
because of the continuity of the partial trace $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}$ in trace norm. Hence $\mathcal{A}$ is compact as a closed subset of a compact set.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- coro-4: body_md -->
\label{coro:compact-additional-marginal-energy}
Assume the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{coro:compactc}. Let
$k\in\mathbb N$. For each $\ell\in[k]$, let
$A_\ell\in\mathcal{L}_\geq(\mathcal{H}_0)$ be a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal{H}_0$, and let
$E_\ell\in[0,+\infty)$. Define
\[
    \mathcal{A}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}
    :=
    \left\{
    (\pi_s)_{s\in S}\in\mathcal{A}:
    \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(
        A_\ell\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi_s
    \right)
    \leq E_\ell
    \quad
    \text{for all }s\in S,\ \ell\in[k]
    \right\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}$ is compact in the norm $
    \|(\,T_s\,)_{s\in S}\|
    :=
    \sum_{s\in S}\|T_s\|_1 $.
<!-- end coro-4 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By Corollary~\ref{coro:compactc}, the set $\mathcal{A}$ is compact in the
product trace norm. Fix $s\in S$ and $\ell\in[k]$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:marginal-energy-closed},
the set
\[
    \left\{
    \pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s):
    \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(
        A_\ell\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi
    \right)
    \leq E_\ell
    \right\}
\]
is closed in the trace-norm topology. Hence
$\mathcal{A}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}$ is the intersection of $\mathcal{A}$ with
finitely many closed sets. Therefore, $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}$ is a closed subset of the
compact set $\mathcal{A}$, and hence is compact.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:quadrature_bounds}
Let $m\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathcal{H}_0,\mathcal{H}$ be separable Hilbert spaces and \(C\) be a quadrature-generated cost on
\(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}\), associated with quadrature generators
\(\{R_j\}_{j\in[2m]}\) on \(\mathcal{H}_0\) and
\(\{S_j\}_{j\in[2m]}\) on \(\mathcal{H}\). Let $H_0:=\sum_{j=1}^{2m} R_j^2$ and $H:=\sum_{j=1}^{2m} S_j^2$ be the corresponding one-body square-sums as in \eqref{intro:eq:one-body-H}. Then, 
\[
    C
    \le
    2\bigl(H_0\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}
    +
    \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes H\bigr),\text{\quad and}\quad
    C+3\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes H
    \ge
    \frac34\,H_0\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}.
\]
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
On the algebraic tensor core
$\mathcal H_R^\infty\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathcal H_S^\infty$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
    &2\sum_{j=1}^{2m}
    \bigl(\|R_j\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}\psi\|^2
    +\|\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes S_j\psi\|^2\bigr)\\
    &\quad-
    \sum_{j=1}^{2m}
    \|(R_j\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes S_j)\psi\|^2\\
    &\qquad=
    \sum_{j=1}^{2m}
    \|(R_j\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}+\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes S_j)\psi\|^2
    \ge0,
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
    &\sum_{j=1}^{2m}\|(R_j\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes S_j)\psi\|^2
    +
    3\sum_{j=1}^{2m}\|\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes S_j\psi\|^2
    -
    \frac34\sum_{j=1}^{2m}\|R_j\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}\psi\|^2\\
    =&
    \sum_{j=1}^{2m}
    \left\|
        \frac12R_j\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}\psi-2\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes S_j\psi
    \right\|^2
    \ge0.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
These quadratic-form inequalities hold on a common form core for
$C$, $H_0\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}$, and $\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes H$; passing to the
closures proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
By assumption~\eqref{eq:exas},
$ \mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)<+\infty$.
Choose a minimizing sequence
\[
\left(
(\pi_s^{(n)})_{s\in[N]}
\right)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}
\subset
\Gamma_{\mathrm{joint}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\]
for the joint formulation~\eqref{eq:joint-primal-setting}, so that
\[
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl(C_s\pi_s^{(n)}\bigr)
\rightarrow
\mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma).
\]
After discarding finitely many terms if necessary, we may assume that
\[
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\bigl(C_s\pi_s^{(n)}\bigr)
\le
 \mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)+1,
\qquad n\in\mathbb{N}.
\]


Fix $s_0\in[N]$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:existenceQOTbary_intro}. We consider the following cases.
\medskip

\noindent

\emph{(i) Cost operators with compact resolvent.}
If $C_{s_0}$ is a cost operator with compact resolvent, define the set
\[
\mathcal{A}_{s_0}:=\Bigl\{\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_{s_0}):\ 
\begin{aligned}[t]
&\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi=\sigma_{s_0},\\
&\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_{s_0}\pi)\le
\bigl(\mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)+1\bigr)/\alpha_{s_0}
\end{aligned}
\Bigr\}.
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:compact1}(i), $\mathcal{A}_{s_0}$ is compact in the
trace-norm topology, and by construction
$\pi_{s_0}^{(n)}\in \mathcal{A}_{s_0}$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$.


\medskip

\noindent
\emph{(ii) Quadrature-generated cost.}
Assume $C_{s_0}$ is a quadrature-generated cost with associated one-body square-sums
$H^{(s_0)}_0$ on $\mathcal{H}_0$ and $H^{(s_0)}$ on $\mathcal{H}_{s_0}$. Define
\[
\mathcal{A}_{s_0}:=\Bigl\{\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_{s_0}):\ 
\begin{aligned}[t]
&\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi=\sigma_{s_0},\\
&\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\big(H^{(s_0)}_0\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_{s_0}}\pi\big)\\
&\qquad\le \tfrac{4}{3}\Bigl(
\tfrac{\mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)+1}{\alpha_{s_0}}
+3\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H^{(s_0)}\sigma_{s_0})\Bigr)
\end{aligned}
\Bigr\}.
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:quadrature_bounds}, we have
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\big(C_{s_0}\pi_{s_0}^{(n)}\big)
\ge \tfrac{3}{4}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\big(H^{(s_0)}_0\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_{s_0}}\pi_{s_0}^{(n)}\big)-3\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H^{(s_0)}\sigma_{s_0}),
\]
since $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi_{s_0}^{(n)}=\sigma_{s_0}$. Hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:compact1}(ii), $\mathcal{A}_{s_0}$ is compact in the trace-norm topology, and $\pi_{s_0}^{(n)}\in \mathcal{A}_{s_0}$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$.


\medskip
In either case, after passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $\pi_{s_0}^{(n)}\to\pi_{s_0}^\ast$ in trace norm. Let
$\rho_n:=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_{s_0}}\pi_{s_0}^{(n)}$ and $\rho^\ast:=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_{s_0}}\pi_{s_0}^\ast$. By trace-norm continuity of the partial trace, $\rho_n\to\rho^\ast$ in trace norm.

For every $s\ne s_0$, one has $\pi_s^{(n)}\in\Gamma(\rho_n,\sigma_s)$. Theorem~\ref{theo:compact} gives a further trace-norm convergent subsequence of $(\pi_s^{(n)})_n$. Since $N$ is finite, successive subsequence extractions yield
$(\pi_s^{(n)})_{s\in[N]}\to(\pi_s^\ast)_{s\in[N]}$ in product trace norm, where $\pi_s^\ast\in\Gamma(\rho^\ast,\sigma_s)$ for every $s\in[N]$.

Moreover, $\rho_n\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\mathcal{H}_0)$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:Hclosed},
$\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_\ell\rho^\ast)\leq E_\ell$ for every $\ell\in[k]$. Hence
$(\pi_s^\ast)_{s\in[N]}\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{joint}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\boldsymbol\sigma)$.


Finally, for each $s\in[N]$, the map $\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)
\longmapsto
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_s\pi)\in[0,+\infty]$ is lower semicontinuous in trace norm. Indeed, by Proposition~\ref{prop:spectral-trunc-positive},
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_s\pi)
=
\sup\Bigl\{
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(B\pi):
B\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s),\
0\le B\le C_s
\Bigr\},
\]
and each map $\pi\mapsto\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(B\pi)$ is trace-norm continuous. Therefore,
\[
\sum_{s\in [N]}\alpha_s\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_s\pi_s^\ast)
\le \liminf_{n\to\infty}\sum_{s\in [N]}\alpha_s\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_s\pi_s^{(n)})
=\mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}),
\]
so $(\pi_s^\ast)_{s\in [N]}$ is optimal. Let $\overline{\rho}:=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi_s^\ast$ for any $s\in[N]$;
this is independent of $s$ by the common-marginal constraint. Then $\overline{\rho}\in\mathrm{Bar}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})$ is a barycenter and
\[
 \mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})
=\min_{\rho\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\mathcal{H}_0)}\ \sum_{s=1}^{N}\alpha_s\,\operatorname{QOT}\!\big(\rho,\sigma_s\mid C_s\big).
\]
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Equip the product space $\prod_{s=1}^N
\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)$ with the maximum product norm $(B_s)_{s\in[N]}\mapsto\max_{s\in[N]}\|B_s\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ and define $f:\prod_{s=1}^N\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)
\rightarrow
(-\infty,+\infty]$ by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:def:f}
f((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
:=
\iota_{\mathcal{B}_\le(\mathbf C)}((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
=
\begin{cases}
0,
&
B_s\le C_s,\quad s\in[N],
\\[1mm]
+\infty,
&
\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
with $\mathcal{B}_\le(\mathbf C)
    :=
    \left\{
    (B_s)_{s=1}^N\in \prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes \mathcal{H}_s):
    B_s\le C_s,\quad s\in[N]
    \right\}$. Define also $g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}:
\prod_{s=1}^N
\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)
\rightarrow
(-\infty,+\infty]$ by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:defg}
g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
:=
\inf_{\mathcal R_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}((B_s)_{s\in[N]})}
\left[
-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
+
\sum_{\ell=1}^k\eta_\ell E_\ell
\right],
\end{equation}
with the convention $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$, where
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal R_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
:=
\Bigl\{
&
\bigl(
(U_s^{(\ell)})_{s\in[N],\,\ell\in[k]},
(V_s)_{s\in[N]},
(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]}
\bigr):
\\
&
U_s^{(\ell)}\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0),\quad
V_s\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_s),\quad
\eta_\ell\ge0,
\\
&
B_s=
\left(
\sum_{\ell=1}^k U_s^{(\ell)}
\right)\oplus V_s,
\qquad s\in[N],
\\
&
-\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}
\le
\eta_\ell A_\ell,
\qquad \ell\in[k]
\Bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The function $f$ is proper and convex, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:gAE-convex-proper} shows that
$g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}$ is proper and convex. By Proposition~\ref{prop:FR-left-identification-constrained},
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&
\inf_{(B_s)_{s\in[N]}
\in
\prod_{s=1}^N
\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)}
\left\{
f((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
+
g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
\right\}
\\
&\qquad
=
-
\sup
\Biggl\{
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
-
\sum_{\ell=1}^k
\eta_\ell E_\ell
:
\bigl(
(U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]},
(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]}
\bigr)
\in\mathsf{Pot}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}(\boldsymbol\sigma)\Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:FR-left-main}
\end{equation}
Thus the left-hand side of the Fenchel--Rockafellar formula is the
negative of the claimed dual value. On the other hand, the conjugate computations in
Propositions~\ref{prop:conjugate-f-cost-constraint}
and~\ref{prop:conjugate-gAE}, together with
Proposition~\ref{prop:FR-right-identification-constrained}, give
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&
\sup_{(\Lambda_s)_{s\in[N]}
\in
\prod_{s=1}^N
\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)^*}
\left\{
-f^*((-\Lambda_s)_{s\in[N]})
-
g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*((\Lambda_s)_{s\in[N]})
\right\}
\\
&\qquad
=
-
\inf_{(\pi_s)_{s\in[N]}
\in
\Gamma_{\mathrm{joint}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_s\pi_s)
\\
&\qquad
=
-
\mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma).
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:FR-right-main}
\end{equation}
Thus the right-hand side is the negative of the joint primal value.

It remains to verify the Fenchel--Rockafellar qualification condition. Fix $\delta>0$ and consider $B_s^0:=-\delta\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s}$ for $s\in[N]$. Taking $U_s^{(\ell)}=0$, $V_s=-\delta\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}$ and $\eta_\ell=0$ shows that $(B_s^0)_{s\in[N]}\in\operatorname{Dom} g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}$. Moreover, since $C_s\ge0$, if $\|B_s-B_s^0\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\frac{\delta}{2}$ for all $s\in[N]$, then $B_s
\le
-\frac{\delta}{2}
\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s}
\le
C_s$ for all $s\in[N]$. Thus $(B_s^0)_{s\in[N]}\in
\operatorname{Dom} f\cap\operatorname{Dom} g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}$,
and $f$ is continuous at this point.

The qualification condition of
Theorem~\ref{app:FRTheorem} is thus satisfied. Applying the
Fenchel--Rockafellar theorem and combining
\eqref{eq:FR-left-main} and \eqref{eq:FR-right-main} yields
\[
\mathcal{B}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
=
\sup
\Biggl\{
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
-
\sum_{\ell=1}^k
\eta_\ell E_\ell
:
\bigl(
(U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]},
(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]}
\bigr)
\in
\mathsf{Pot}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\Biggr\},
\]
which is precisely
\eqref{eq:energy-constrained-duality-barycenter}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:energy-constrained-barycenter-duality}
with $k=1$, $A_1=0$, and $E_1=0$. The primal problem is then
unconstrained, while the dual compatibility condition becomes
$\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_sU_s\geq0$.

For any admissible family, set
$U:=\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_sU_s$ and replace $U_s$ by $U_s-U$
for every $s\in[N]$. Since $U\geq0$, the cost inequalities remain
valid, the weighted sum of the first-marginal potentials becomes
zero, and the dual objective is unchanged. Conversely, every
family with weighted sum zero is admissible for the preceding
inequality constraint. Hence the two dual suprema coincide,
which proves \eqref{eq:unconstrained-barycenter-duality}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:quadrature_bounds}, for any
$(\pi_s)_{s\in[N]}\in
\Gamma_{\mathrm{joint}}(\boldsymbol\sigma)$
with common barycentric marginal $\rho$,
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_s\pi_s)
\le
2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(
H_0^{(s)}\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi_s
\right)
+
2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(
H^{(s)}\,\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi_s
\right)=
2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H_0^{(s)}\rho)
+
2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H^{(s)}\sigma_s).
\]
The last equality holds since $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi_s=\rho$ and $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi_s=\sigma_s$. Therefore,
\[
\mathcal{B}_0^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\le
2\left(
M+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H^{(s)}\sigma_s)
\right),
\]
where $M:=\inf_{\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0)}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H_0^{(s)}\rho)$.


On the other hand, let $\overline\rho$ be a barycenter and let
$(\pi_s^\ast)_{s\in[N]}$ be optimal couplings with common
barycentric marginal $\overline\rho$. By the lower bound in
Proposition~\ref{prop:quadrature_bounds},
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C_s\pi_s^\ast)
\ge
\frac34\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H_0^{(s)}\overline\rho)
-
3\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H^{(s)}\sigma_s).
\]
Summing over $s$ gives
\[
\mathcal{B}_0^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\ge
\frac34
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}
\left( H_0^{(s)}\overline\rho\right)
-
3
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H^{(s)}\sigma_s).
\]
Combining the two bounds yields
\begin{equation}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}
\left( H_0^{(s)}\overline\rho
\right)
\le
\frac83 M
+
\frac{20}{3}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H^{(s)}\sigma_s)
<+\infty.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
Let $N\in\mathbb N$, $\boldsymbol{\alpha}:=(\alpha_s)_{s\in[N]}$ be positive weights satisfying $\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s = 1$. Let $\mathcal{H}_0$ and $(\mathcal{H}_s)_{s\in[N]}$ be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}:=(\sigma_s)_{s\in[N]}$ with $\sigma_s\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_s)$,
and $\mathbf C:=(C_s)_{s\in[N]}$ be a family of cost operators.

Then the unconstrained QOT barycenter problem
\eqref{eq:unconstrained-barycenter-primal}
admits a minimizer and satisfies the duality formula
\eqref{eq:unconstrained-barycenter-duality}.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
Let $m,N\in\mathbb N$, let $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_s)_{s\in[N]}$ be
positive weights satisfying $\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s=1$, and let
$\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}=(\hat\sigma_s)_{s\in[N]}$ with
$\hat\sigma_s\in\mathcal{S}(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$ such that
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\hat{\mathsf{H}}_{\mathrm{osc}}\hat\sigma_s)<+\infty,
\qquad s\in[N].
\]
Then the $2$-quantum Wasserstein barycenter problems
\eqref{eq:tau-barycenter-intro} admit minimizers and satisfy the duality
formula~\eqref{eq:unconstrained-barycenter-duality}. Moreover, every barycenter
$\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau$ has finite energy with respect to the harmonic
oscillator Hamiltonian:
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\hat{\mathsf{H}}_{\mathrm{osc}}\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau)<\infty.
\]
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- deff-5: body_md -->
\label{def:finite-canonical-second-moments}
We define
\[
\mathcal{S}_2^R(\mathcal{H})
:=
\left\{
\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}):
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\mathsf H_{\mathbf R}\rho)<+\infty
\right\}.
\]
For $\rho\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(\mathcal{H})$, its canonical mean vector
$\mathbf m_\rho=(m_{\rho,1},\ldots,m_{\rho,2m})^\top\in\mathbb R^{2m}$
and covariance matrix
$\Sigma_\rho=[(\Sigma_\rho)_{jk}]_{j,k\in[2m]}
\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ are defined by
$m_{\rho,j}:=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\rho R_j)$ and
\[
(\Sigma_\rho)_{jk}
:=
\frac12
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(
\rho\left[
(R_j-m_{\rho,j}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{H})(R_k-m_{\rho,k}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{H})
+
(R_k-m_{\rho,k}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{H})(R_j-m_{\rho,j}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{H})
\right]
\right).
\]
<!-- end deff-5 -->
<!-- deff-6: body_md -->
\label{def:weyl-characteristic-gaussian-state}
For every $\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$, its Weyl characteristic function is
\[
\chi_\rho(\boldsymbol\xi)
:=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\bigl(\rho W(\boldsymbol\xi)\bigr),
\qquad
\boldsymbol\xi\in\mathbb R^{2m}.
\]
For $\rho\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(\mathcal{H})$, following
\cite[Sec.~III.A]{HolevoWerner2001BosonicGaussian} and
\cite[Sec.~12.3.2]{Holevo2019QSCI}, the state $\rho$ is called Gaussian if
\[
\chi_\rho(\boldsymbol\xi)
=
\exp\!\left(
i\mathbf m_\rho^\top\boldsymbol\xi
-\frac12\boldsymbol\xi^\top\Sigma_\rho\boldsymbol\xi
\right),
\qquad
\boldsymbol\xi\in\mathbb R^{2m}.
\]
We denote the set of Gaussian states on $\mathcal{H}$ by $\mathcal{S}^G(\mathcal{H})$.
<!-- end deff-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:rs-uncertainty-canonical}
For every $\rho\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(\mathcal{H})$,
\[
\Sigma_\rho+\frac{i}{2}\Theta\succeq0.
\]
Conversely, if
$\Sigma\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ satisfies
$\Sigma+\frac{i}{2}\Theta\succeq0$, then for every
$\mathbf m\in\mathbb R^{2m}$ there exists a Gaussian state with mean
$\mathbf m$ and covariance $\Sigma$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- deff-7: body_md -->
\label{def:gaussian-projection}
For $\rho\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(\mathcal{H})$, the \emph{Gaussian projection}
$\mathcal G(\rho)$ is the unique Gaussian state with the same mean and
covariance as $\rho$:
\[
\mathbf m_{\mathcal G(\rho)}=\mathbf m_\rho,
\qquad
\Sigma_{\mathcal G(\rho)}=\Sigma_\rho.
\]
<!-- end deff-7 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:williamson}
For every
$\Sigma\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ with $\Sigma\succ0$, there exist
$S\in\operatorname{Sp}(2m,\mathbb R)$ and positive numbers
$\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_m$, unique up to permutation, such that
\[
\Sigma
=
S\left(
\bigoplus_{j=1}^m{}_D\nu_j\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\right)S^\top.
\]
The numbers $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_m$ are called the symplectic eigenvalues
of $\Sigma$.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- deff-8: body_md -->
\label{def:gaussian-unitary}
A unitary $\hat U\in\mathcal U(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$ is called Gaussian if its action on the canonical variables is affine symplectic, namely $\hat U^\dagger\hat{\mathbf R}\hat U=S\hat{\mathbf R}+\mathbf z$ for some $S\in\operatorname{Sp}(2m,\mathbb R)$ and
$\mathbf z\in\mathbb R^{2m}$. Consequently,
$$
\mathbf m_{\hat U\rho\hat U^\dagger}
=
S\mathbf m_\rho+\mathbf z,
\qquad
\Sigma_{\hat U\rho\hat U^\dagger}
=
S\Sigma_\rho S^\top.
$$
<!-- end deff-8 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:reduction-moments}
The reduced states
$\hat\pi_1:=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_2\hat\pi$ and
$\hat\pi_2:=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_1\hat\pi$ have moments
\[
\mathbf m_{\hat\pi_1}=\mathbf m_1,
\qquad
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_1}=\Sigma_{11},
\qquad
\mathbf m_{\hat\pi_2}=\mathbf m_2,
\qquad
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_2}=\Sigma_{22}.
\]
If $\hat\pi$ is Gaussian, then both reduced states are Gaussian.
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
The moment identities follow from
Proposition~\ref{prop:partialtrace-unbounded}. For Gaussianity, the
reduced characteristic functions are obtained by restriction,
$\chi_{\hat\pi_1}(\boldsymbol\xi)
=
\chi_{\hat\pi}(\boldsymbol\xi,0)$ and $\chi_{\hat\pi_2}(\boldsymbol\eta)
=
\chi_{\hat\pi}(0,\boldsymbol\eta)$, and are therefore Gaussian.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:stateTrC}
Let $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and let
$\hat\pi\in
\mathcal{S}_2^R\bigl(
L_2(\mathbb R^m)\otimes L_2^{(\tau)}(\mathbb R^m)
\bigr)$
have mean and covariance as above. Then
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\bigl(\hat C^{(\tau)}\hat\pi\bigr)
=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_{11})
+
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_{22})
-
2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A)
+
\|\mathbf m_1-\mathbf m_2\|^2.
\]
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Expanding the quadratic cost \eqref{eq:tau-cost} gives, for each
$j\in[2m]$,
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left[
\bigl(
\hat R_j\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}
-
\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}\otimes\hat R_j^{(\tau)}
\bigr)^2
\hat\pi
\right]
=
(\Sigma_{11})_{jj}
+
(\Sigma_{22})_{jj}
-
2A_{jj}
+
(m_{1,j}-m_{2,j})^2.
\]
Summing over $j$ proves the formula.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:gaussian-projection-lower}
Let
$\hat\rho,\hat\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$. Then, for every
$\tau\in\{\pm1\}$,
\[
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\bigl(
\mathcal G(\hat\rho),
\mathcal G(\hat\sigma)
\bigr)
\leq
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma).
\]
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
For any
$\hat\pi\in\Gamma_\tau(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma)$,
Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction-moments} implies that
$\mathcal G(\hat\pi)$ is a coupling of
$\mathcal G(\hat\rho)$ and $\mathcal G(\hat\sigma)$ in the
$\tau$-formulation. Since Gaussian projection preserves the mean and
covariance,
Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC} gives
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\bigl(
\hat C^{(\tau)}\mathcal G(\hat\pi)
\bigr)
=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\bigl(
\hat C^{(\tau)}\hat\pi
\bigr).
\]
Taking the infimum over $\hat\pi$ proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:Gaussian-opt-plan}
Let
$\hat\rho^G,\hat\sigma^G\in\mathcal{S}^G(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$. Then, for every
$\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, the corresponding $2$-QW transport problem admits a
Gaussian optimal coupling.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Let $\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}}$ be an optimal coupling, whose existence
follows from the general existence results for the two $2$-QW
transport problems
\cite{caglioti2021towards,DPaTre19}. Since its Gaussian marginals have finite canonical second moments,
the preceding observation implies that
$\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}}$ also has finite canonical second moments.
Hence its Gaussian projection
$\mathcal G(\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}})$ is well defined and has the same
Gaussian marginals by
Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction-moments}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC} gives
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\bigl(
\hat C^{(\tau)}
\mathcal G(\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}})
\bigr)
=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\bigl(
\hat C^{(\tau)}
\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}}
\bigr).
\]
Hence $\mathcal G(\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}})$ is a Gaussian optimal
coupling.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:gaussian-projection-barycenter}
Let $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and let $\hat\rho$ be a $2$-QW barycenter of
$\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^G$. Then $\mathcal G(\hat\rho)$ is also a
barycenter and
\[
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\bigl(\mathcal G(\hat\rho),\hat\sigma_s^G\bigr)
=
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\bigl(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s^G\bigr),
\qquad s\in[N].
\]
Moreover, if
$\hat\pi_s\in\Gamma_\tau(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s^G)$ is any optimal
coupling, then $\mathcal G(\hat\pi_s)$ is an optimal Gaussian coupling
between $\mathcal G(\hat\rho)$ and $\hat\sigma_s^G$.
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Since $\mathcal G(\hat\sigma_s^G)=\hat\sigma_s^G$,
Proposition~\ref{prop:gaussian-projection-lower} gives
\[
\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s\, \operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\mathcal G(\hat\rho),\hat\sigma_s^G)
\leq
\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s\, \operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s^G).
\]
As $\hat\rho$ is a barycenter, equality must hold and
$\mathcal G(\hat\rho)$ is also a barycenter. Since every
$\alpha_s>0$ and the corresponding pairwise inequalities hold
termwise, equality of the weighted sums implies
\[
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\bigl(\mathcal G(\hat\rho),\hat\sigma_s^G\bigr)
=
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\bigl(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s^G\bigr),
\qquad s\in[N].
\]

Let $\hat\pi_s$ be optimal between $\hat\rho$ and
$\hat\sigma_s^G$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction-moments},
$\mathcal G(\hat\pi_s)$ is a coupling between
$\mathcal G(\hat\rho)$ and $\hat\sigma_s^G$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC} gives
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(
\hat C^{(\tau)}\mathcal G(\hat\pi_s)
\right)
=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(
\hat C^{(\tau)}\hat\pi_s
\right).
\]
The preceding pairwise equality therefore shows that
$\mathcal G(\hat\pi_s)$ is optimal.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:gaussian-pairwise-covariance}
Let $\hat\rho^G,\hat\sigma^G\in\mathcal{S}^G(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$ have means
$\mathbf m,\mathbf m_\sigma$ and covariances
$\Sigma,\Sigma_\sigma$, respectively. Then, for
$\tau\in\{\pm1\}$,
\[
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\hat\rho^G,\hat\sigma^G)
=
\|\mathbf m-\mathbf m_\sigma\|^2
+
\min_{A\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_\sigma)}
\left\{
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma)+\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_\sigma)-2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A)
\right\}.
\]
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:Gaussian-opt-plan}, an optimal coupling may be
chosen Gaussian. By Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction-moments}, its mean
is $(\mathbf m,\mathbf m_\sigma)$ and its covariance has block form
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma&A\\
A^\top&\Sigma_\sigma
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_\sigma).
\]
Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC} then gives the stated objective.
Conversely, every
$A\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_\sigma)$ determines an admissible
Gaussian bipartite state with these moments, whose marginals are
$\hat\rho^G$ and $\hat\sigma^G$. Hence the optimization over Gaussian
couplings is exactly the stated finite-dimensional problem.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
By the existence result of Section~\ref{sec:qot-bary}, the barycenter
problem admits a minimizer. Proposition~\ref{prop:gaussian-projection-barycenter}
shows that the Gaussian projection of any barycenter is again a
barycenter. Thus a Gaussian barycenter exists.

Let $\hat\rho^G$ be a Gaussian state with mean
$\mathbf m\in\mathbb R^{2m}$ and covariance
$\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_m^{\mathrm Q}$. Applying
Proposition~\ref{prop:gaussian-pairwise-covariance} to each input gives
\[
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\,
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\hat\rho^G,\hat\sigma_s^G)
=
\min_{\substack{
A_s\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s),\\
s\in[N]}}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\left[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma)+\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_s)-2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)
+
\|\mathbf m-\mathbf m_s\|^2
\right].
\]
Therefore the Gaussian barycenter problem is equivalent to
\begin{equation}
\min_{\substack{
\mathbf m\in\mathbb R^{2m},\,
\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_m^{\mathrm Q},\\
A_s\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s),\ s\in[N]}}
\left\{
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma)
+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_s)-2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)\bigr)
+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\|\mathbf m-\mathbf m_s\|^2
\right\}.
\end{equation}

Set $\overline{\mathbf m}:=\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\mathbf m_s$. The identity
\[
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\|\mathbf m-\mathbf m_s\|^2
=
\|\mathbf m-\overline{\mathbf m}\|^2
+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\|\mathbf m_s-\overline{\mathbf m}\|^2
\]
shows that the mean is uniquely minimized at
$\mathbf m=\overline{\mathbf m}$. After minimizing over the mean variable, the Gaussian barycenter problem reduces to \eqref{eq:qw2cov}. Thus every Gaussian barycenter has mean
$\overline{\mathbf m}$ and covariance equal to the first component of
an optimizer of \eqref{eq:qw2cov}. Conversely,
every optimizer of \eqref{eq:qw2cov}, together with
the mean $\overline{\mathbf m}$, determines a Gaussian barycenter.
This proves the theorem.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:arbitrary-barycenter-covariance}
Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and let $\hat\rho$ be any, possibly
non-Gaussian, barycenter of $\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^G$. Then $\mathbf m_{\hat\rho}=\overline{\mathbf m}$. Moreover, if for each $s\in[N]$, $\hat\pi_s\in\Gamma_\tau(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s^G)$ is any optimal
coupling and $A_s$ denotes its cross-covariance, then
\[
\bigl(
\Sigma_{\hat\rho},A_1,\ldots,A_N
\bigr)
\]
is an optimizer of the covariance problem
\eqref{eq:qw2cov}.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:gaussian-projection-barycenter},
$\mathcal G(\hat\rho)$ is a Gaussian barycenter. Hence
Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian-barycenter-intro} gives
$\mathbf m_{\hat\rho}
=
\mathbf m_{\mathcal G(\hat\rho)}
=
\overline{\mathbf m}$.

For each $s$, Proposition~\ref{prop:gaussian-projection-barycenter}
also shows that $\mathcal G(\hat\pi_s)$ is an optimal Gaussian coupling
between $\mathcal G(\hat\rho)$ and $\hat\sigma_s^G$. Gaussian
projection preserves the covariance of $\hat\pi_s$, so
$\mathcal G(\hat\pi_s)$ has block covariance
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma_{\hat\rho}&A_s\\
A_s^\top&\Sigma_s
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since $\mathcal G(\hat\rho)$ is a Gaussian barycenter, the covariance
reduction above implies that
$(\Sigma_{\hat\rho},A_1,\ldots,A_N)$ attains
\eqref{eq:qw2cov}.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:covdual}
Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and assume \eqref{eq:faithful-inputs}. For $Z_r\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\mathrm{sa}}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$, we denote its
$2m\times2m$ blocks by $(Z_r)_{ij}$, $i,j\in\{1,2\}$. Recall that
$\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}$ denotes the minimum value of
\eqref{eq:qw2cov}. If $k<N$, define
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf D_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}
:=&
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_s)
+
\max_{\substack{
Z_r\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}}),\ r\in[k],\\
\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{12}=-\alpha_r\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m},\ r\in[k]}}
\Bigg\{
-\sum_{r=1}^k
\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
Z_r^\dagger
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&0\\
0&\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\end{pmatrix}
\right]
\\
&
-
\sup_{\substack{
\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_m^{\mathrm Q},\\
A_s\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s),\
s=k+1,\ldots,N}}
\left\{
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\left(
\sum_{r=1}^k\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{11}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\right)\Sigma
\right]
+
2\sum_{s=k+1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)
\right\}
\Bigg\}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:covariance-dual-faithful}
\end{equation}
If $k=N$, define instead 
\begin{equation} 
\begin{aligned} 
\mathsf D_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}} := \sum_{s=1}^{N}\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_s) + \max_{\substack{ Z_s\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}}),\ s\in[N],\\ \operatorname{Re} (Z_s)_{12}=-\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m},\ s\in[N],\\ \sum_{s=1}^N\operatorname{Re} (Z_s)_{11}=\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}}} \left\{ -\sum_{s=1}^N \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[ Z_s^\dagger \begin{pmatrix} \frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&0\\ 0&\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m 
\end{pmatrix} \right] \right\}. 
\end{aligned} \label{eq:covariance-dual-fully-faithful} \end{equation} 

Strong duality holds:
$\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}=
\mathsf D_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}$. Moreover, the corresponding dual maximum is attained.
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
By the definitions of 
$f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ and $g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$,
\[
\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}
=
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_s)
+
\inf_{\mathbf V}
\left\{
f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau(\mathbf V)+g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau(\mathbf V)
\right\}.
\]

Choose $t>\hbar/2$ and set $\mathbf V_0:=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cov}}(t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m},0,\ldots,0)$. By \eqref{eq:faithful-inputs},
$(\mathbf V_0)_r+
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&0\\
0&\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m\end{smallmatrix}\right)
\succ0$ for all $r\in[k]$, so $\mathbf V_0\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{Dom}f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)$.
Moreover, $\mathbf V_0\in\operatorname{Dom}g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$: if $k<N$,
this follows from $0\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m},\Sigma_s)$ for $k+1\leq s\leq N$, while for $k=N$ it follows directly from the definition of $g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$. Since $f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ vanishes on a neighborhood of $\mathbf V_0$, it is continuous at $\mathbf V_0$.
Fenchel--Rockafellar Theorem~\ref{app:FRTheorem} therefore yields
\[
\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}
=
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_s)
+
\max_{\mathbf Z}
\left\{
-(f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(-\mathbf Z)
-
(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)
\right\},
\]
and the maximum is attained. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:dualfunccov},
$(f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(-\mathbf Z)<+\infty$ requires
$Z_r\succeq0$ for every $r\in[k]$, while
$(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)<+\infty$ requires $\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{12}
=-\alpha_r\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$ for all $r\in[k]$. 
Substituting the formulas for $(f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*$ and $(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*$
from Proposition~\ref{prop:dualfunccov} gives
\eqref{eq:covariance-dual-faithful} when $k<N$. When $k=N$, the
remaining supremum over
$\Sigma\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ is finite if and only if $\sum_{s=1}^N\operatorname{Re} (Z_s)_{11}=\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$, in which case it equals zero. This gives
\eqref{eq:covariance-dual-fully-faithful}. Hence, in either case,
$\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}=\mathsf D_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}$, and
the corresponding dual maximum is attained.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:faithful-complementary-slackness}
Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and assume \eqref{eq:faithful-inputs}. Let $\mathbf Z^\star=(Z_r^\star)_{r\in[k]}$ be any dual optimizer from Proposition~\ref{prop:covdual}. Then, for every optimizer
$(\Sigma^\star,A_1^\star,\ldots,A_N^\star)$ of
\eqref{eq:qw2cov},
\begin{equation}
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma^\star+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&A_r^\star\\
(A_r^\star)^\top&
\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\end{pmatrix}
Z_r^\star
=
0,
\qquad r\in[k].
\label{eq:faithful-complementary-slackness}
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Let $\mathbf V^\star:=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cov}}(\Sigma^\star,A_1^\star,\ldots,A_k^\star)$. By strong duality and optimality, equality holds in the Fenchel
inequality for $f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$, hence
\[
f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau(\mathbf V^\star)
+
(f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(-\mathbf Z^\star)
=
-\operatorname{Re}\sum_{r=1}^k
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\bigl[(Z_r^\star)^\dagger V_r^\star\bigr].
\]
Since $f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau(\mathbf V^\star)=0$, the formula for
$(f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*$ gives
\[
\sum_{r=1}^k
\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
(Z_r^\star)^\dagger
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma^\star+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&A_r^\star\\
(A_r^\star)^\top&
\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\end{pmatrix}
\right]
=
0.
\]
Each summand is nonnegative. Hence every summand vanishes, and
\eqref{eq:faithful-complementary-slackness} follows from the fact that
$P,Q\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(PQ)=0$ imply $PQ=0$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:faithful-covariance-uniqueness}
Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and assume \eqref{eq:faithful-inputs}. Then there
exists a unique $\overline\Sigma_\tau\in\mathrm{Cov}_m^{\mathrm Q}$ such that every optimizer
$(\Sigma^\star,A_1^\star,\ldots,A_N^\star)$ of
\eqref{eq:qw2cov} satisfies $\Sigma^\star=\overline\Sigma_\tau$.
Moreover, for every $r\in[k]$, there exists a unique $\overline A_{r,\tau}\in\mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)$ such that every optimizer satisfies $A_r^\star=\overline A_{r,\tau}$.
<!-- end prop-13 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Let
$(\Sigma^{(j)},A_1^{(j)},\ldots,A_N^{(j)})$, $j=1,2$, be two
optimizers of \eqref{eq:qw2cov}, and let
$\mathbf Z^\star=(Z_r^\star)_{r\in[k]}$ be any dual optimizer from
Proposition~\ref{prop:covdual}. Fix $r\in[k]$. By
Corollary~\ref{cor:faithful-complementary-slackness},
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma^{(j)}+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&A_r^{(j)}\\
(A_r^{(j)})^\top&
\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\end{pmatrix}
Z_r^\star
=
0,
\qquad
j=1,2.
\]
Set $\Delta\Sigma:=\Sigma^{(1)}-\Sigma^{(2)}$ and $\Delta A_r:=A_r^{(1)}-A_r^{(2)}$. Subtracting the two identities gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\Delta\Sigma&\Delta A_r\\
\Delta A_r^\top&0
\end{pmatrix}
Z_r^\star
=
0.
\]
The $(2,2)$-block yields $\Delta A_r^\top(Z_r^\star)_{12}=0$. Since $\Delta A_r$ is real and $\operatorname{Re}(Z_r^\star)_{12}=-\alpha_r\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$, we obtain $0
=
\Delta A_r^\top\operatorname{Re}(Z_r^\star)_{12}
=
-\alpha_r\Delta A_r^\top$. Hence $\Delta A_r=0$. The $(1,2)$-block then gives $\Delta\Sigma(Z_r^\star)_{12}=0$, and therefore
$0=\Delta\Sigma\operatorname{Re}(Z_r^\star)_{12}=-\alpha_r\Delta\Sigma$. Thus $\Delta\Sigma=0$.

Since $r\in[k]$ was arbitrary, the same argument gives uniqueness of
the cross-covariance associated with every faithful input.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:faithful-unique-gaussian-minimizer}
Assume \eqref{eq:faithful-inputs}. For each $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, there exists exactly one Gaussian $2$-QW barycenter of the inputs
$\hat\sigma_1^G,\ldots,\hat\sigma_N^G$. We denote it by
$\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^G$. Its mean is $\overline{\mathbf m}=\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\mathbf m_s$, and its covariance is the unique matrix $\overline\Sigma_\tau$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:faithful-covariance-uniqueness}.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian-barycenter-intro}, every Gaussian barycenter has mean
$\overline{\mathbf m}=\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\mathbf m_s$, and its
covariance is the first component of an optimizer of
\eqref{eq:qw2cov}. Conversely, every optimizer of
\eqref{eq:qw2cov}, together with the mean
$\overline{\mathbf m}$, determines a Gaussian barycenter.

Proposition~\ref{prop:faithful-covariance-uniqueness} shows that the
covariance component of every optimizer is the same matrix
$\overline\Sigma_\tau$. Hence every Gaussian barycenter has mean
$\overline{\mathbf m}$ and covariance $\overline\Sigma_\tau$.
Since a Gaussian state is uniquely determined by its mean and
covariance, the Gaussian barycenter is unique.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- deff-9: body_md -->
\label{def:gaussian-channel}
Recall that a quantum channel between Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_1$ and
$\mathcal{H}_2$ is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal T^{(1)}(\mathcal{H}_1)\rightarrow
\mathcal T^{(1)}(\mathcal{H}_2)$.
Let $m_2\in\mathbb{N}$ and $m_1\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$. A quantum channel
$\Phi_G:\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{m_1}))\rightarrow
\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{m_2}))$
is called Gaussian if there exist
$\mathbb{X}_G\in\mathbb R^{2m_2\times2m_1}$,
$\mathbb Y_G\in\mathcal{M}_{2m_2,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$, and
$\mathbf m_G\in\mathbb R^{2m_2}$ such that, for every
$\hat\rho\in\mathcal{S}(L_2(\mathbb R^{m_1}))$ and every
$\mathbf z\in\mathbb R^{2m_2}$,
\begin{equation}
\chi_{\Phi_G(\hat\rho)}(\mathbf z)
=
\chi_{\hat\rho}(\mathbb{X}_G^\top\mathbf z)
\exp\left(
i\mathbf m_G^\top\mathbf z
-\frac12\mathbf z^\top\mathbb Y_G\mathbf z
\right).
\label{eq:gaussian-channel-characteristic-function}
\end{equation}
For parameters of this form, complete positivity is equivalent to
$\mathbb Y_G+\frac{i\hbar}{2}
(\Omega_{m_2}-\mathbb{X}_G\Omega_{m_1}\mathbb{X}_G^\top)\succeq0$.
We call $\mathbb{X}_G$ the phase-space transformation matrix of
$\Phi_G$.
<!-- end deff-9 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:faithful-gaussian-deconvolution}
Let $\Phi_G:\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{m_1}))\rightarrow
\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{m_2}))$
be a Gaussian channel with phase-space transformation matrix
$\mathbb{X}_G$. If $\mathbb{X}_G$ has full column rank, then $\Phi_G$
is injective on quantum states. Moreover, if $\Phi_G(\hat\rho)$ is
Gaussian, then $\hat\rho$ is Gaussian.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
The zero-mode case is immediate. Otherwise,
$\mathbb{X}_G^\top$ is surjective, so there exists a linear map
$\mathbb J:\mathbb R^{2m_1}\rightarrow\mathbb R^{2m_2}$ such that
$\mathbb{X}_G^\top\mathbb J=\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m_1}$.
By \eqref{eq:gaussian-channel-characteristic-function}, for every
$\hat\rho$ and $\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^{2m_1}$,
\[
\chi_{\hat\rho}(\mathbf u)
=
\chi_{\Phi_G(\hat\rho)}(\mathbb J\mathbf u)
\exp\left(
-i\mathbf m_G^\top\mathbb J\mathbf u
+
\frac12
\mathbf u^\top
\mathbb J^\top\mathbb Y_G\mathbb J
\mathbf u
\right).
\]
Thus the output characteristic function uniquely determines the input
characteristic function, proving injectivity. If
$\Phi_G(\hat\rho)$ is Gaussian, the right-hand side is Gaussian in
$\mathbf u$. In particular, its restrictions
$t\mapsto\chi_{\hat\rho}(t e_j)$ are one-dimensional Gaussian
characteristic functions, so all canonical second moments of
$\hat\rho$ are finite. Hence
$\hat\rho\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{m_1}))$, and
Definition~\ref{def:weyl-characteristic-gaussian-state} implies that
$\hat\rho$ is Gaussian.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- prop-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:dual-support-gaussian-source}
Let $\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_{2m}^{\mathrm Q}$ and
$Z\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$ satisfy the covariance slackness relation
\[
\left(
\Sigma+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)Z=0.
\]
Then $\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Re} Z)$ is even. Set $q:=\frac12\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Re} Z)$ and fix $\mathbf m\in\mathbb R^{4m}$. There exists a fixed Gaussian channel $\Phi_G:
\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m-q}))
\rightarrow
\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ with phase-space transformation matrix $\mathbb X_\Phi$ satisfying $\operatorname{Ran}(\mathbb X_\Phi)=\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)$. Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&
\left\{
\hat\pi\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m})) :
\begin{gathered}
\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}=\mathbf m,\\[-2pt]
\left(
\Sigma_{\hat\pi}+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)Z=0
\end{gathered}
\right\}
\\[-2pt]
&\qquad=
\left\{
\Phi_G(\hat\eta) :
\hat\eta\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m-q})),
\ \mathbf m_{\hat\eta}=0
\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
<!-- end prop-14 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Since $\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_{2m}^{\mathrm Q}$, Theorem~\ref{thm:rs-uncertainty-canonical} yields a Gaussian state
$\hat\pi_0\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ with mean $\mathbf m$ and
covariance $\Sigma$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:faithful-dual-Williamson} to $(\hat\pi_0,\Sigma,Z)$. It follows that $\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Re} Z)$ is even. Therefore $q:=\frac12\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Re} Z)\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:faithful-dual-Williamson} also provides a symplectic matrix $S=(S_0\ S_1)\in\operatorname{Sp}(4m,\mathbb R)$, where
$S_0\in\mathbb R^{4m\times2q}$ and
$S_1\in\mathbb R^{4m\times2(2m-q)}$, such that, for some $d_1,\ldots,d_q>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:SZS}
S^\top ZS
=
\bigoplus_{j=1}^q{}_D
\frac{d_j}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}
1&-i\\
i&1
\end{pmatrix}
\oplus_D 0_{2(2m-q)},
\end{equation}
and $\operatorname{Ran}(S_1)=\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)$. Fix a Gaussian unitary $\hat U_S$ implementing $S$. Define
\[
\Phi_G(\hat\rho)
:=
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}\!\left( \frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m}{\hbar} \right)\hat U_S
\left(
|0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes q}\otimes\hat\rho
\right)
\hat U_S^\dagger W_{\mathrm{CCR}}\!\left( \frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m}{\hbar} \right)^\dagger.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:fock-ancilla-Gaussian-channel},
$\Phi_G$ is a Gaussian channel whose phase-space transformation
matrix is $\mathbb X_\Phi=S_1$. Consequently, $\operatorname{Ran}(\mathbb X_\Phi)=\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)$.


We now prove the claimed equality of sets. Let
$\hat\pi\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ satisfy $\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}=\mathbf m$ and $\left(
\Sigma_{\hat\pi}
+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)Z=0$. Define $\hat\pi'
:=
\hat U_S^\dagger
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}\!\left( \frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m}{\hbar} \right)^\dagger
\hat\pi
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}\!\left( \frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m}{\hbar} \right)
\hat U_S$. Then $\hat\pi'$ has zero mean, and its covariance is $V:=S^{-1}\Sigma_{\hat\pi}S^{-\top}$. By symplecticity of $S$, the covariance slackness relation becomes $\left(
V+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)S^\top ZS=0$.


For $j\in[q]$, let $v_j:=e_{2j-1}+ie_{2j}$. The range of the $j$-th nonzero block of $S^\top ZS$ in \eqref{eq:SZS} is spanned by $v_j$. Hence $\left(
V+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)v_j=0$. Since $\Omega_{2m}v_j=iv_j$, this gives $Vv_j=\frac{\hbar}{2}v_j$. Because $V$ is real and symmetric, it follows that $Ve_{2j-1}=\frac{\hbar}{2}e_{2j-1}$ and $Ve_{2j}=\frac{\hbar}{2}e_{2j}$ for $j\in[q]$, and therefore $V
=
\frac{\hbar}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2q}
\oplus_D V_{\mathrm{res}}$. Each of the first $q$ one-mode marginals of $\hat\pi'$ thus has
zero mean and covariance $(\hbar/2)\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2$, and is consequently the
Fock ground state. Iterating the pure-marginal factorization, we
obtain $\hat\pi'=
|0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes q}\otimes\hat\eta$ for some $\hat\eta\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m-q}))$ with zero mean. It follows directly from the definition of $\Phi_G$ that $\hat\pi=\Phi_G(\hat\eta)$. This proves the inclusion from left to right.

Conversely, let $\hat\eta\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m-q}))$ with $\mathbf m_{\hat\eta}=0$ and set $\hat\pi:=\Phi_G(\hat\eta)$. By construction of $\Phi_G$, $\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}=\mathbf m$ and $\Sigma_{\hat\pi}
=
S\left(
\frac{\hbar}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2q}
\oplus_D\Sigma_{\hat\eta}
\right)S^\top$. Moreover, the canonical form \eqref{eq:SZS} of $S^\top ZS$ gives $\left[
\frac{\hbar}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2q}
\oplus_D\Sigma_{\hat\eta}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right]
S^\top ZS
=0$. Conjugating this identity by $S$ and $S^{-1}$ yields $\left(
\Sigma_{\hat\pi}
+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)Z=0$. Thus $\hat\pi$ belongs to the set on the left, proving the reverse
inclusion.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- prop-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:saturated-face-reconstruction}
Let $Z\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$, and let $\Psi_G:
\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))
\rightarrow
\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^\ell))$ be a Gaussian channel with phase-space transformation matrix $\mathbb X_\Psi\in\mathbb R^{2\ell\times4m}$. Assume $\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)\cap\ker(\mathbb X_\Psi)=\{0\}$. If
$\hat\pi_1,\hat\pi_2\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ have the same mean and
satisfy $\left(
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_j}+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)Z=0$ for $j=1,2$ and $\Psi_G(\hat\pi_1)=\Psi_G(\hat\pi_2)$, then $\hat\pi_1=\hat\pi_2$. Moreover, if
$\hat\pi\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ satisfies $\left(
\Sigma_{\hat\pi}+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)Z=0$ and $\Psi_G(\hat\pi)$ is Gaussian, then $\hat\pi$ is Gaussian.
<!-- end prop-15 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Set $q:=\frac12\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Re} Z)$. For the first statement, apply
Proposition~\ref{prop:dual-support-gaussian-source} with
$\Sigma=\Sigma_{\hat\pi_1}$ and with the common mean of
$\hat\pi_1$ and $\hat\pi_2$. There exists a common Gaussian channel
$\Phi_G$, with phase-space transformation matrix $\mathbb X_\Phi$,
and zero-mean states $\hat\eta_1,\hat\eta_2$ such that $\hat\pi_j=\Phi_G(\hat\eta_j)$ and $\operatorname{Ran}(\mathbb X_\Phi)=\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)$ for $j=1,2$.
Since $\dim\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)=4m-2q=2(2m-q)$, $\mathbb X_\Phi$ has full column rank.

The composition $\Psi_G\circ\Phi_G$ is Gaussian with phase-space
transformation matrix $\mathbb X_\Psi\mathbb X_\Phi$. If
$\mathbb X_\Psi\mathbb X_\Phi\mathbf u=0$, then $\mathbb X_\Phi\mathbf u
\in
\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)\cap\ker(\mathbb X_\Psi)$, and hence $\mathbb X_\Phi\mathbf u=0$ by the assumed intersection
condition. Since $\mathbb X_\Phi$ has full
column rank, $\mathbf u=0$. Thus
$\mathbb X_\Psi\mathbb X_\Phi$ has full column rank. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:faithful-gaussian-deconvolution},
$\Psi_G\circ\Phi_G$ is injective. Therefore
