$\Psi_G(\hat\pi_1)=\Psi_G(\hat\pi_2)$ implies
$\hat\eta_1=\hat\eta_2$, and hence $\hat\pi_1=\hat\pi_2$.

For the second statement, apply
Proposition~\ref{prop:dual-support-gaussian-source} with
$\Sigma=\Sigma_{\hat\pi}$ and $\mathbf m=\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}$. Then
$\hat\pi=\Phi_G(\hat\eta)$ for some zero-mean $\hat\eta$, with
$\operatorname{Ran}(\mathbb X_\Phi)=\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)$. The same argument shows that
$\mathbb X_\Psi\mathbb X_\Phi$ has full column rank. Since $\Psi_G(\hat\pi)
=
(\Psi_G\circ\Phi_G)(\hat\eta)$ is Gaussian, Lemma~\ref{lem:faithful-gaussian-deconvolution} implies
that $\hat\eta$ is Gaussian. Hence
$\hat\pi=\Phi_G(\hat\eta)$ is Gaussian.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:saturated-face-marginal-reconstruction}
Let $Z\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)
\cap
\left(
\mathbb R^{2m}\oplus\{0\}^{2m}
\right)
=
\{0\}.
\label{eq:second-marginal-observable-support}
\end{equation}
If $\hat\pi_1,\hat\pi_2\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ have the same mean,
satisfy
$(\Sigma_{\hat\pi_j}+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m})Z=0$,
$j=1,2$,
and have the same second marginal, then
$\hat\pi_1=\hat\pi_2$.

Moreover, if $\hat\pi\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ satisfies
$(\Sigma_{\hat\pi}+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m})Z=0$
and its second marginal is Gaussian, then
$\hat\pi$ is Gaussian.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
The partial trace $\Psi_G:=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_1$ is a Gaussian channel with
phase-space transformation matrix
$\operatorname{pr}_2:=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0_{2m}&\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$.
Since
$\ker(\operatorname{pr}_2)
=
\mathbb R^{2m}\oplus\{0\}^{2m}$,
condition \eqref{eq:second-marginal-observable-support} gives
$\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)\cap\ker(\operatorname{pr}_2)=\{0\}$.
The result follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:saturated-face-reconstruction}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:faithful-barycenter-rigidity} 
Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and assume \eqref{eq:faithful-inputs}. Let 
$\hat\rho_\tau$ be any $2$-QW barycenter of 
$\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^G$. Then 
\[ 
\mathbf m_{\hat\rho_\tau} 
= 
\overline{\mathbf m}, 
\qquad 
\Sigma_{\hat\rho_\tau} 
= 
\overline\Sigma_\tau, 
\qquad 
\mathcal G(\hat\rho_\tau) 
= 
\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^G, 
\] 
where $\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^G$ is the unique Gaussian barycenter 
from Corollary~\ref{cor:faithful-unique-gaussian-minimizer}. 
 
Moreover, fix $r\in[k]$, and let $\hat\pi_{\tau,r}$ be any optimal 
coupling between $\hat\rho_\tau$ and the faithful input 
$\hat\sigma_r^G$. Then the cross-covariance of 
$\hat\pi_{\tau,r}$ is $\overline A_{r,\tau}$ from 
Proposition~\ref{prop:faithful-covariance-uniqueness}, and hence 
\begin{equation} 
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_{\tau,r}} 
= 
\begin{pmatrix} 
\overline\Sigma_\tau&\overline A_{r,\tau}\\ 
\overline A_{r,\tau}^\top&\Sigma_r 
\end{pmatrix}. 
\label{eq:faithful-input-coupling-covariance} 
\end{equation} 
Furthermore, for every dual optimizer 
$\mathbf Z^\star=(Z_r^\star)_{r\in[k]}$ from 
Proposition~\ref{prop:covdual}, 
\begin{equation} 
\begin{pmatrix} 
\overline\Sigma_\tau+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m& 
\overline A_{r,\tau}\\ 
\overline A_{r,\tau}^\top& 
\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m 
\end{pmatrix} 
Z_r^\star 
= 
0. 
\label{eq:faithful-input-coupling-complementarity} 
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
By Corollary~\ref{cor:arbitrary-barycenter-covariance}, 
$\mathbf m_{\hat\rho_\tau}=\overline{\mathbf m}$ and 
$\Sigma_{\hat\rho_\tau}$ is the covariance component of an optimizer 
of \eqref{eq:qw2cov}. Hence 
Proposition~\ref{prop:faithful-covariance-uniqueness} gives 
$\Sigma_{\hat\rho_\tau}=\overline\Sigma_\tau$. Since Gaussian 
projection preserves first and second moments, 
$\mathcal G(\hat\rho_\tau)$ has mean $\overline{\mathbf m}$ and 
covariance $\overline\Sigma_\tau$, and therefore 
$\mathcal G(\hat\rho_\tau)=\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^G$. 
 
Fix $r\in[k]$ and the prescribed optimal coupling 
$\hat\pi_{\tau,r}$, and denote its cross-covariance by $A_r$. 
Choose arbitrary optimal couplings with the remaining inputs, thereby 
completing $\hat\pi_{\tau,r}$ to a family of optimal couplings. 
Corollary~\ref{cor:arbitrary-barycenter-covariance} implies that the 
corresponding tuple 
$(\Sigma_{\hat\rho_\tau},A_1,\ldots,A_N)$ is an optimizer of 
\eqref{eq:qw2cov}. Hence 
Proposition~\ref{prop:faithful-covariance-uniqueness} gives 
$A_r=\overline A_{r,\tau}$, proving 
\eqref{eq:faithful-input-coupling-covariance}. 
 
Finally, 
Corollary~\ref{cor:faithful-complementary-slackness}, applied to the 
same covariance optimizer and any dual optimizer 
$\mathbf Z^\star$, gives 
\[ 
\begin{pmatrix} 
\Sigma_{\hat\rho_\tau}+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&A_r\\ 
A_r^\top& 
\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m 
\end{pmatrix} 
Z_r^\star 
= 
0. 
\] 
Substituting 
$\Sigma_{\hat\rho_\tau}=\overline\Sigma_\tau$ and 
$A_r=\overline A_{r,\tau}$ yields 
\eqref{eq:faithful-input-coupling-complementarity}.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- prop-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:faithful-input-standard-CCR} 
Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and $r\in[k]$. Let $\hat\rho_\tau$ be a $2$-QW 
barycenter of $\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^G$, let 
$\hat\pi_{\tau,r}$ be an optimal coupling between $\hat\rho_\tau$ and 
the faithful input $\hat\sigma_r^G$, and let 
$\mathbf Z^\star=(Z_r^\star)_{r\in[k]}$ be a dual optimizer from 
Proposition~\ref{prop:covdual}. Define 
\[ 
\widetilde\pi_{\tau,r} 
:= 
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{L_2(\mathbb R^m)}\otimes J_{\tau,m}\bigr) 
\hat\pi_{\tau,r} 
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{L_2(\mathbb R^m)}\otimes J_{\tau,m}\bigr)^\dagger, 
\qquad 
\widetilde Z_r^\star 
:= 
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}\bigr) 
Z_r^\star 
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}\bigr)^\top. 
\] 
Then $\widetilde\pi_{\tau,r}$ is a state on 
$L_2(\mathbb R^m)\otimes L_2(\mathbb R^m)$ whose first marginal is 
$\hat\rho_\tau$ and whose second marginal is Gaussian. Moreover, 
$\widetilde Z_r^\star\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$ and 
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\left(
\Sigma_{\widetilde\pi_{\tau,r}}
+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)
\widetilde Z_r^\star
&=0,\\
\bigl(\operatorname{Re}\widetilde Z_r^\star\bigr)_{12}
&=-\alpha_rF_{\tau,m},\\
\ker\bigl(\operatorname{Re}\widetilde Z_r^\star\bigr)
\cap
\left(
\mathbb R^{2m}\oplus\{0\}^{2m}
\right)
&=\{0\}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:faithful-standard-certificate} 
\end{equation}
<!-- end prop-16 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:tau-standard-CCR-identification}, 
conjugation of the second subsystem by $J_{\tau,m}$ transforms the 
canonical variables according to 
$\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}$. Hence 
\[ 
\Sigma_{\widetilde\pi_{\tau,r}} 
= 
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}\bigr) 
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_{\tau,r}} 
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}\bigr)^\top. 
\] 
Since the conjugation acts only on the second subsystem, the first 
marginal remains $\hat\rho_\tau$, while the second marginal is the 
standard-CCR image of $\hat\sigma_r^G$ and is therefore Gaussian. 
 
By Corollary~\ref{cor:faithful-barycenter-rigidity}, 
\[ 
\left[ 
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_{\tau,r}} 
+ 
\frac{i\hbar}{2} 
\bigl( 
\Omega_m\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_m) 
\bigr) 
\right] 
Z_r^\star 
= 
0. 
\] 
Since $Z_r^\star\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$, congruence by 
$\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}$ gives 
$\widetilde Z_r^\star\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$. Using 
\begin{align*} 
\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{4m}&=(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m})^\top 
(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}) 
,\\ 
\Omega_{2m}&=\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}\bigr) 
\bigl( 
\Omega_m\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_m) 
\bigr) 
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\oplus_DF_{\tau,m}\bigr)^\top 
, 
\end{align*} 
we obtain $\left( 
\Sigma_{\widetilde\pi_{\tau,r}} 
+ 
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m} 
\right) 
\widetilde Z_r^\star = 0$. Moreover, the upper-right block of $\widetilde Z_r^\star$ is 
$(Z_r^\star)_{12}F_{\tau,m}^\top$. Since $F_{\tau,m}$ is real 
symmetric and 
$\operatorname{Re}(Z_r^\star)_{12}=-\alpha_r\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$, $\bigl(\operatorname{Re}\widetilde Z_r^\star\bigr)_{12} 
= 
-\alpha_rF_{\tau,m}$. 
 
Finally, suppose 
$(\mathbf x,\mathbf0)\in 
\ker(\operatorname{Re}\widetilde Z_r^\star)$. Taking the second block row gives $-\alpha_rF_{\tau,m}^\top\mathbf x=0$. Since $\alpha_r>0$ and $F_{\tau,m}$ is invertible, $\mathbf x=0$. Hence  $\ker(\operatorname{Re}\widetilde Z_r^\star) 
\cap 
\left( 
\mathbb R^{2m}\oplus\{0\}^{2m} 
\right) 
= 
\{0\}$.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
As above, after relabeling the inputs if necessary, we assume that $\hat\sigma_1^G,\ldots,\hat\sigma_k^G$ are faithful and choose $s_0\in[k]$.

Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, and let 
$\hat\rho_\tau$ be any $2$-QW barycenter of 
$\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^G$. Let 
$\hat\pi_{\tau,s_0}$ be an optimal coupling between 
$\hat\rho_\tau$ and $\hat\sigma_{s_0}^G$, and fix a dual optimizer 
$\mathbf Z^\star=(Z_r^\star)_{r\in[k]}$ from 
Proposition~\ref{prop:covdual}. 
 
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:faithful-input-standard-CCR} to 
$\hat\pi_{\tau,s_0}$. The resulting state 
$\widetilde\pi_{\tau,s_0}$ satisfies 
\[ 
\left( 
\Sigma_{\widetilde\pi_{\tau,s_0}} 
+ 
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m} 
\right) 
\widetilde Z_{s_0}^\star 
= 
0 
\] 
and $\ker(\operatorname{Re}\widetilde Z_{s_0}^\star) \cap \left( 
\mathbb R^{2m}\oplus\{0\}^{2m} 
\right) 
= 
\{0\}$. 

By Proposition~\ref{prop:faithful-input-standard-CCR}, the second 
marginal of $\widetilde\pi_{\tau,s_0}$ is Gaussian. Therefore 
Corollary~\ref{cor:saturated-face-marginal-reconstruction} implies 
that $\widetilde\pi_{\tau,s_0}$ is Gaussian, and hence so is its first 
marginal $\hat\rho_\tau$. 
 
By Corollary~\ref{cor:faithful-barycenter-rigidity}, $\mathcal G(\hat\rho_\tau) 
= 
\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^G$. Since $\hat\rho_\tau$ is Gaussian, $\hat\rho_\tau 
= 
\mathcal G(\hat\rho_\tau) 
= 
\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^G$. Since $\hat\rho_\tau$ was arbitrary, the $2$-QW barycenter is unique 
and equals $\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^G$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- deff-10: body_md -->
\label{def:wigner-function}
For $\hat\rho\in\mathcal{S}^G(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$, its Wigner function is
defined by
\[
\mathbb W_{\hat\rho}(\mathbf z)
:=
\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{2m}}
\int_{\mathbb R^{2m}}
e^{-i\boldsymbol\xi^\top\mathbf z}
\chi_{\hat\rho}(\boldsymbol\xi)\,
d\boldsymbol\xi.
\]
If $\hat\rho$ has mean $\mathbf m$ and covariance $\Sigma$, then
$\mathbb W_{\hat\rho}$ is the density of
$\mathcal N(\mathbf m,\Sigma)$.
<!-- end deff-10 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$. We first compare the quantum and classical covariance problems. If
$(\Sigma,A_1,\ldots,A_N)$ is quantum feasible, then
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma&A_s\\
A_s^\top&\Sigma_s
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}
\bigl(\Omega_m\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_m)\bigr)
\succeq0,
\qquad s\in[N].
\]
Restricting the corresponding quadratic forms to real vectors gives
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\Sigma&A_s\\A_s^\top&\Sigma_s\end{smallmatrix}\right)\succeq0$ for every $s\in[N]$.
Thus every quantum-feasible tuple is classically feasible, and hence
$\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}^\hbar
\geq\mathsf P_{0,\mathrm{cov}}$.

Conversely, let
$(\overline\Sigma,A_1^0,\ldots,A_N^0)$ be an optimizer of
\eqref{eq:classical-gaussian-barycenter-cov}. Since $\Sigma_s\succ0$,
the Schur complement gives
$\overline\Sigma-A_s^0\Sigma_s^{-1}(A_s^0)^\top\succeq0$ for every
$s\in[N]$.

For
$0<\hbar\leq\min_{s\in[N]}\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_s)$, one has
$\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m\succ0$ and $
\left\|
\left(
\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\right)^{-1}
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq
\frac{2}{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_s)}$. Using the resolvent identity $A^{-1}-B^{-1}=A^{-1}(B-A)B^{-1}$ and $\|\Omega_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1$, we therefore obtain
\[
\left\|
\left(
\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\right)^{-1}
-
\Sigma_s^{-1}
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq
\frac{\hbar}{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_s)^2},
\]
uniformly in $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$. Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left\|
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
-
A_s^0
\left[
\left(
\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\right)^{-1}
-
\Sigma_s^{-1}
\right]
(A_s^0)^\top
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq
\hbar
\left(
\frac12+
\frac{\|A_s^0\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2}
{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_s)^2}
\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Choose $c>
\max_{s\in[N]}
\left\{
\frac12+
\frac{\|A_s^0\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2}
{\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_s)^2}
\right\}$ and set
$\Sigma_\hbar:=\overline\Sigma+c\hbar\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\Sigma_\hbar+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
-
A_s^0
\left(
\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\right)^{-1}
(A_s^0)^\top
\\
&=
\overline\Sigma
-
A_s^0\Sigma_s^{-1}(A_s^0)^\top
+
c\hbar\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
-
A_s^0
\left[
\left(
\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\right)^{-1}
-
\Sigma_s^{-1}
\right]
(A_s^0)^\top
\succeq0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence, by the Schur complement,
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma_\hbar+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&A_s^0\\
(A_s^0)^\top&
\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\end{pmatrix}
\succeq0,
\qquad s\in[N].
\]
Thus $(\Sigma_\hbar,A_1^0,\ldots,A_N^0)$ is quantum feasible for both
values of $\tau$. Evaluating the objective and combining with the
opposite inequality above gives
\[
0
\leq
\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}^\hbar
-
\mathsf P_{0,\mathrm{cov}}
\leq
2mc\,\hbar,
\]
which proves the convergence of the optimal values.

We next prove convergence of the minimizing covariances. Let
$(\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar),
A_{1,\tau}^\hbar,\ldots,A_{N,\tau}^\hbar)$ be an optimal quantum
tuple. It is also classically feasible. The standard factorization of
positive block matrices \cite[Prop.~1.3.2]{Bhatia2007PDM} and the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_{s,\tau}^\hbar)
\leq
\sqrt{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)}
\sqrt{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_s},
\qquad s\in[N].
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathsf P_{\tau,\mathrm{cov}}^\hbar
\geq
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)
-
2\sqrt{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)}
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\sqrt{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_s}
+
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_s.
\]
Since the optimal values are uniformly bounded for sufficiently small
$\hbar$, the family
$\{\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)\}$ is bounded. Classical feasibility
and the same block-factorization argument imply that
$\{A_{s,\tau}^\hbar\}$ is bounded for every $s\in[N]$.

Let $\hbar_n\rightarrow0$. Passing to a subsequence if necessary, we may assume $\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar_n)\rightarrow\Sigma_*$ and $A_{s,\tau}^{\hbar_n}\rightarrow A_s^*$ for all $s\in[N]$. The limit tuple $(\Sigma_*,A_1^*,\ldots,A_N^*)$ is classically feasible. By continuity
of the objective and the convergence of the optimal values,
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_*)
+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\bigl(\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_s)-2\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s^*)\bigr)
=
\mathsf P_{0,\mathrm{cov}}.
\]
Thus $\Sigma_*$ minimizes
\eqref{eq:classical-gaussian-barycenter-cov}. By uniqueness,
$\Sigma_*=\overline\Sigma$. Since every convergent subsequence has the
same limit, $\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)
\rightarrow
\overline\Sigma$.


Finally,
$\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^\hbar$ is Gaussian with mean
$\overline{\mathbf m}$ and covariance
$\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)$. Hence, by
Definition~\ref{def:wigner-function},
\[
\mathbb{W}_{\hat{\overline\rho}_\tau^\hbar}(\mathbf z)\,d\mathbf z
=
\mathcal N\bigl(
\overline{\mathbf m},
\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)
\bigr)(d\mathbf z).
\]
Since the means are fixed and
$\overline\Sigma_\tau(\hbar)\rightarrow\overline\Sigma$, the
corresponding characteristic functions converge pointwise. Hence the
Wigner distributions converge weakly to
$\mathcal N(\overline{\mathbf m},\overline\Sigma)$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:pure-input-coherent-barycenter}
Let
$\hat\sigma_1,\ldots,\hat\sigma_N\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$
be pure states with means
$\mathbf m_1,\ldots,\mathbf m_N$, and set
$\overline{\mathbf m}:=\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\mathbf m_s$.
Then, for every $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, the corresponding $2$-QW
barycenter is unique and is the coherent state
$\ket{\overline{\mathbf m}}\!\bra{\overline{\mathbf m}}$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:finitesecondemomentrho}, every barycenter has
finite canonical second moments. Let
$\hat\rho\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$. Since the prescribed marginal
$\hat\sigma_s$ is pure, every coupling between $\hat\rho$ and
$\hat\sigma_s$ factorizes. Hence its cross-covariance vanishes, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2(\hat\rho,\hat\sigma_s)
={}&
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_{\hat\rho})
+
\|\mathbf m_{\hat\rho}-\overline{\mathbf m}\|^2+
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s
\left(
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_{\hat\sigma_s})
+
\|\mathbf m_s-\overline{\mathbf m}\|^2
\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The last sum is independent of $\hat\rho$, while
\[
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma_{\hat\rho})
+
\|\mathbf m_{\hat\rho}-\overline{\mathbf m}\|^2
=
\sum_{j=1}^{2m}
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\hat\rho
\left(
\hat R_j-\overline m_j\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}
\right)^2
\right].
\]
The operator on the right is a Weyl displacement of the harmonic
oscillator Hamiltonian and has
$\ket{\overline{\mathbf m}}\!\bra{\overline{\mathbf m}}$ as its unique ground state. Hence the
barycenter is uniquely equal to
$\ket{\overline{\mathbf m}}\!\bra{\overline{\mathbf m}}$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- prop-17: body_md -->
\label{prop:thermal-barycenter-uniqueness}
Let $\hat\sigma_s^{\mathrm{th}}$, $s\in[N]$, be displaced thermal
Gaussian states with means $\mathbf m_s$ and covariances
$w_s\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$, where $w_s\geq\hbar/2$. Then, for every
$\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, the corresponding $2$-QW barycenter is unique
among all quantum states.
<!-- end prop-17 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
If $w_r>\hbar/2$ for some $r\in[N]$, then
$\hat\sigma_r^{\mathrm{th}}$ is faithful, and uniqueness follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:faithful-global-uniqueness-intro}. Otherwise
$w_s=\hbar/2$ for every $s\in[N]$, so all prescribed states are
coherent and therefore pure. In this case uniqueness follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:pure-input-coherent-barycenter}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- prop-18: body_md -->
\leavevmode\par
\label{prop:qotcovid1}
Let
$\hat\rho^{\mathrm{th}},\hat\sigma^{\mathrm{th}}
\in\mathcal{S}(L_2(\mathbb R^m))$
be displaced thermal states with means
$\mathbf m_{\hat\rho},\mathbf m_{\hat\sigma}$ and covariances
$w_{\hat\rho}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m},w_{\hat\sigma}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$, respectively, where
$w_{\hat\rho},w_{\hat\sigma}\geq\hbar/2$. Without loss of generality,
assume $w_{\hat\rho}\geq w_{\hat\sigma}$. Then
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,+1}^2
(\hat\rho^{\mathrm{th}},\hat\sigma^{\mathrm{th}})
=
2m
\left[
\sqrt{w_{\hat\rho}-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
-
\sqrt{w_{\hat\sigma}-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2
+
2m\hbar
+
\|\mathbf m_{\hat\rho}-\mathbf m_{\hat\sigma}\|^2,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,-1}^2
(\hat\rho^{\mathrm{th}},\hat\sigma^{\mathrm{th}})
=
2m
\left[
\sqrt{w_{\hat\rho}+\frac{\hbar}{2}}
-
\sqrt{w_{\hat\sigma}-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2
+
\|\mathbf m_{\hat\rho}-\mathbf m_{\hat\sigma}\|^2.
\end{equation}
<!-- end prop-18 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian-barycenter-intro}, there exists a
Gaussian barycenter with mean
$\overline{\mathbf m}:=\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\mathbf m_s$, whose
covariance is the covariance component of an optimizer of
\eqref{eq:qw2cov}.

Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ and let
$(\Sigma,A_1,\ldots,A_N)$ be such an optimal covariance tuple. For
each $s\in[N]$, the covariance of the corresponding Gaussian optimal
coupling has the form
\[
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_s^G}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma&A_s\\
A_s^\top&w_s\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
By Corollary~\ref{coro:multimode-isotropic-reduction}, feasibility
implies feasibility of the isotropized block
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma)}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\\
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
&
w_s\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}
\bigl(
\Omega_m\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_m)
\bigr)
\succeq0.
\]
Since isotropization preserves
$\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma)$ and $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)$,
Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC} shows that the corresponding displaced
thermal Gaussian state with mean $\overline{\mathbf m}$ and covariance
$\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\Sigma)}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$ is also a barycenter. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:thermal-barycenter-uniqueness}, the barycenter is
unique. Hence it is necessarily a displaced thermal Gaussian state
with mean $\overline{\mathbf m}$ and covariance
$\overline w_\tau\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$ for some
$\overline w_\tau\geq\hbar/2$.

For $\tau=+1$, Proposition~\ref{prop:qotcovid1} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{B}_{+1}(\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^{\mathrm{th}}\mid\boldsymbol{\alpha})
={}&
2m
\min_{w\geq\hbar/2}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\left[
\sqrt{w-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
-
\sqrt{w_s-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2+
2m\hbar
+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\|\overline{\mathbf m}-\mathbf m_s\|^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The unique minimizer is $
\overline w_{+1}
=
\left[
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\sqrt{w_s-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2
+
\frac{\hbar}{2}$.

For $\tau=-1$, Proposition~\ref{prop:qotcovid1} gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:wctr-D2}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{B}_{-1}(\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^{\mathrm{th}}\mid\boldsymbol{\alpha})
={}&
2m
\min_{w\geq\hbar/2}
\Bigg\{
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{w_s<w}
\alpha_s
\left[
\sqrt{w+\frac{\hbar}{2}}
-
\sqrt{w_s-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2\\
&\quad+
\sum_{w_s\geq w}
\alpha_s
\left[
\sqrt{w_s+\frac{\hbar}{2}}
-
\sqrt{w-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2
\end{aligned}
\Bigg\}
\\
&+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\|\overline{\mathbf m}-\mathbf m_s\|^2.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
By uniqueness of the barycenter,
$\overline w_{-1}$ is the unique minimizer of
\eqref{eq:wctr-D2}.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- coro-5: body_md -->
\label{coro:densitycentervalue}
Let $m,N\in\mathbb N$,
$\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_s)_{s\in[N]}$ be positive weights
satisfying $\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s=1$, and let
$\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^{\mathrm{th}}:=(\hat\sigma_s^{\mathrm{th}})_{s\in[N]}$ be
displaced thermal Gaussian states with means $\mathbf m_s$ and covariances
$w_s\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$. 
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{B}_{+1}
(\hat{\boldsymbol\sigma}^{\mathrm{th}}\mid\boldsymbol{\alpha})
={}&
\sum_{s=1}^N
\left\{
2m\alpha_s
\left[
\sqrt{\overline w_{+1}-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
-
\sqrt{w_s-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2
+
\alpha_s
\|\overline{\mathbf m}-\mathbf m_s\|^2
\right\}
+
2m\hbar
\\
={}&
2m
\left(
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\left(
w_s-\frac{\hbar}{2}
\right)
-
\left[
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\sqrt{w_s-\frac{\hbar}{2}}
\right]^2
\right)
\\
&+
\left(
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\|\mathbf m_s\|^2
-
\left\|
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\mathbf m_s
\right\|^2
\right)
+
2m\hbar.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
<!-- end coro-5 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:tensorization-barycenter}
Fix $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$. Let $r,N\in\mathbb{N}$ and, for each $j\in[r]$,
let $m_j\in\mathbb{N}$. For $j\in[r]$ and $s\in[N]$, let $\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}\in\mathcal{S}\bigl(L_2(\mathbb R^{m_j})\bigr)$ be states with common weights $\alpha_s>0$ satisfying $\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s=1$. Suppose that
$\hat\rho_j\in\mathcal{S}(L_2(\mathbb R^{m_j}))$ is a $2$-QW barycenter of
$\{\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}\}_{s\in[N]}$ with these weights. Then $\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\rho_j$ is a $2$-QW barycenter of $\left\{
\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}
\right\}_{s\in[N]}$ on $\bigotimes_{j=1}^rL_2(\mathbb R^{m_j})
\simeq L_2(\mathbb R^{m_1+\cdots+m_r})$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Let $\hat\rho$ be an arbitrary state on the product system and let
$\hat\rho^{(j)}$ denote its $j$th marginal. Since the quadratic cost
is the sum of the costs on the individual factors, taking the
corresponding factor marginals of any admissible coupling gives
\[
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\left(
\hat\rho,
\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}
\right)
\geq
\sum_{j=1}^r
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\left(
\hat\rho^{(j)},\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}
\right).
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\left(
\hat\rho,
\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}
\right)
&\geq
\sum_{j=1}^r
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\left(
\hat\rho^{(j)},\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}
\right)
\\
&\geq
\sum_{j=1}^r
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\left(
\hat\rho_j,\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}
\right),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second inequality follows from the barycenter property of
each $\hat\rho_j$.

If one of the factor barycenter values on the right-hand side is
$+\infty$, this lower bound makes the conclusion immediate. We may
therefore assume that all factor barycenter values are finite.

Conversely, fix $\varepsilon>0$. For every $s\in[N]$ and $j\in[r]$,
choose an $\varepsilon$-optimal coupling
$\hat\pi_{s,j}^{\varepsilon}$ between
$\hat\rho_j$ and $\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}$. Then
$\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\pi_{s,j}^{\varepsilon}$ is an admissible
coupling between
$\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\rho_j$ and
$\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}$, and additivity of the
quadratic cost gives
\[
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\left(
\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\rho_j,
\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}
\right)
\leq
\sum_{j=1}^r
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,\tau}^2
\left(
\hat\rho_j,\hat\sigma_s^{(j)}
\right)
+
r\varepsilon.
\]
After multiplying by $\alpha_s$, summing over $s\in[N]$, and letting
$\varepsilon\to0$, we obtain the reverse inequality. Hence
$\bigotimes_{j=1}^r\hat\rho_j$ is a barycenter.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:nonfaithful-boundary}
For $w\geq\hbar/2$, let $\hat\sigma_w^{\mathrm{th}}\in\mathcal{S}\bigl(L_2(\mathbb R)\bigr)$
denote the centered one-mode thermal state with covariance $w\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2$.
By Corollary~\ref{cor:thermal-barycenter-intro}, the equal-weight
one-mode $2$-QW barycenter of
$\hat\sigma_{3\hbar/2}^{\mathrm{th}}$ and
$\hat\sigma_{\hbar/2}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is
$\hat\sigma_{3\hbar/4}^{\mathrm{th}}$ for $\tau=+1$ and
$\hat\sigma_{\hbar}^{\mathrm{th}}$ for $\tau=-1$.

Consider the $2$-QW barycenter problem with inputs
\[
\hat\sigma_1
=
\hat\sigma_{3\hbar/2}^{\mathrm{th}}
\otimes
\hat\sigma_{\hbar/2}^{\mathrm{th}},
\qquad
\hat\sigma_2
=
\hat\sigma_{\hbar/2}^{\mathrm{th}}
\otimes
\hat\sigma_{3\hbar/2}^{\mathrm{th}},
\qquad
\alpha_1=\alpha_2=\frac12.
\]
These are centered Gaussian states with covariances
$\Sigma_1=\frac{\hbar}{2}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}3\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&0\\0&\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and
$\Sigma_2=\frac{\hbar}{2}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&0\\0&3\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$.
Thus both inputs are partially pure and nonfaithful.

\emph{Gaussian nonuniqueness.}
For $t\in[-1,1]$, let $\hat\rho_t^\tau$ be the centered Gaussian state
with covariance
\[
\overline\Sigma_t^{+}
=
\frac{\hbar}{4}
\begin{pmatrix}
3\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2\\
t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&3\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\overline\Sigma_t^{-}
=
\frac{\hbar}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}
2\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2\\
t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&2\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For $|t|\leq1$, these matrices belong to $\mathrm{Cov}_2^{\mathrm Q}$,
and the one-mode marginals of $\hat\rho_t^\tau$ are
$\hat\sigma_{3\hbar/4}^{\mathrm{th}}$ for $\tau=+1$ and
$\hat\sigma_{\hbar}^{\mathrm{th}}$ for $\tau=-1$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:nonfaithful-boundary-couplings}, for each
$\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, $t\in[-1,1]$, and $s\in\{1,2\}$, there exists an
optimal coupling between $\hat\rho_t^\tau$ and $\hat\sigma_s$
attaining the corresponding tensorized one-mode cost. Hence
$\hat\rho_t^\tau$ is an equal-weight $2$-QW barycenter of
$\hat\sigma_1$ and $\hat\sigma_2$. Since
$\overline\Sigma_t^\tau$ varies with $t$, this gives a continuum of
distinct Gaussian barycenters. At $t=0$,
$\hat\rho_0^\tau$ is
$(\hat\sigma_{3\hbar/4}^{\mathrm{th}})^{\otimes2}$ for $\tau=+1$
and $(\hat\sigma_{\hbar}^{\mathrm{th}})^{\otimes2}$ for $\tau=-1$,
namely the product barycenter from
Lemma~\ref{lem:tensorization-barycenter}.

\emph{Non-Gaussian barycenters.}
The $2$-QW barycenter objective is convex in the barycentric state:
if $\hat\rho_1$ and $\hat\rho_2$ are $2$-QW barycenters, convex
combinations of their optimal couplings show that
$\lambda\hat\rho_1+(1-\lambda)\hat\rho_2$ is again a $2$-QW
barycenter for every $\lambda\in[0,1]$. Thus, for $t\in(0,1]$,
\[
\hat\omega_t^\tau
:=
\frac12\hat\rho_t^\tau+\frac12\hat\rho_{-t}^\tau
\]
is a barycenter. Since $\overline\Sigma_t^\tau$ is affine in $t$,
$\mathbf m_{\hat\omega_t^\tau}=0$ and
$\Sigma_{\hat\omega_t^\tau}=\overline\Sigma_0^\tau$.
However, $\hat\omega_t^\tau$ is non-Gaussian, being a nontrivial
mixture of two centered Gaussian states with distinct covariance
matrices. Thus $\hat\omega_t^\tau$ and the Gaussian barycenter
$\hat\rho_0^\tau$ are distinct barycenters with identical first and
second canonical moments.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- prop-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:purely}
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable Hilbert space, and let $A\in\mathcal{L}_S(\mathcal{H})$ be a self-adjoint operator. Then $A$ has compact resolvent if and only if it has a purely discrete spectrum; that is, $\mathrm{spec}(A)$ consists only of eigenvalues of finite multiplicity with no accumulation point in \(\mathbb R\).
<!-- end prop-19 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:cost-compact-resolvent}
Let \(\mathcal{H}\) be a separable Hilbert space, 
\(C\in\mathcal{L}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H})\) be a nonnegative operator with compact resolvent and $\mathrm{spec}(C)$ be the spectrum of $C$ counting multiplicity. Then 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:discrete-confining}
    \#\{\lambda\in\mathrm{spec}(C):\ \lambda<r\}<\infty,
    \qquad \text{for all } r>0 .
\end{equation}
Equivalently, if \(\mathcal{H}\) is infinite-dimensional, the eigenvalues of \(C\),
counted with multiplicity, can be ordered as $0\le \lambda_1\le \lambda_2\le\cdots$ with $\lambda_j\to+\infty$.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:purely}, \(C\) has purely discrete spectrum. Therefore, the conclusion follows from $C\geq0$.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lemma:boundedHcompact} Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable Hilbert space and $(\rho_j)_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\subset\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ be a sequence of states. Consider $H\in\mathcal{L}_\geq(\mathcal{H})$ with compact resolvent. If there exists $A\in\mathbb R$ such that $0\le \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho_j)\le A$ for all $j\in\mathbb{N}$, then there exists a subsequence $(\rho_{j_k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ converging in trace norm to some $\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$, and \[ 0\le \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho)\le A. \] 

Equivalently, the sublevel set $\{\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}):\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho)\le A\}$ is trace-norm compact.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- prop-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:Hclosed}
Let \(\mathcal{H}\) be a separable Hilbert space and \(H\in\mathcal{L}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H})\) be a nonnegative self-adjoint operator. Then the extended energy functional
\[
    \mathcal E_H:\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})\to[0,+\infty],
    \qquad
    \mathcal E_H(\rho):=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho),
\]
is affine and lower semicontinuous with respect to the trace-norm topology. Equivalently, if \(\rho_j\to\rho\) in trace norm, then
\[
    \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho)
    \le
    \liminf_{j\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho_j).
\]
Consequently, for every \(A\in[0,+\infty)\), the energy sublevel set $\left\{
    \rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}):\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho)\le A
    \right\}$ is closed in the trace-norm topology.
<!-- end prop-20 -->
<!-- theo-1: body_md -->
\label{theo:compact} Let \(\mathcal{H}_1\) and \(\mathcal{H}_2\) be separable Hilbert spaces, and let \(\rho \in \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1)\) and \(\sigma \in \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_2)\) be density operators. Consider a sequence \((\pi_n)_{n\geq1} \subset \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1 \otimes \mathcal{H}_2)\) of quantum couplings such that \(\pi_n \in \Gamma(\rho_n, \sigma_n)\), where \(\rho_n \to \rho\) and \(\sigma_n \to \sigma\) in trace norm. Then there exists a subsequence $(\pi_{n_k})_{k\ge1}$ and a coupling $\pi\in\Gamma(\rho,\sigma)$ such that \[ \pi_{n_k}\ \to\ \pi\quad\text{in trace norm}. \]
<!-- end theo-1 -->
<!-- prop-21: body_md -->
\label{prop:marginal-energy-closed}
Let $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$ be separable Hilbert spaces, and let
$H\in\mathcal{L}_\geq(\mathcal{H}_1)$ be a nonnegative self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal{H}_1$. For $c\in[0,+\infty)$,
define
\[
    \mathcal C_c:=\left\{
    \pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2):
    \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left[
        H\,(\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\pi)
    \right]
    \leq c
    \right\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal C_c$ is closed with respect to the trace norm.
<!-- end prop-21 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Recall from Proposition~\ref{prop:Hclosed} that, for every nonnegative
self-adjoint operator $H$ on $\mathcal{H}_1$, the energy sublevel set $\mathfrak S_{H,c}(\mathcal{H}_1)
    :=
    \left\{
    \rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1):
    \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(H\rho)\leq c
    \right\}$ is closed in the trace-norm topology.

The partial trace $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}:
    \mathcal{T}^{(1)}_S(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)
    \to
    \mathcal{T}^{(1)}_S(\mathcal{H}_1)$ is trace-norm continuous. Moreover,
\[
    \mathcal C_c
    =
    \left(\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}\right)^{-1}
    \left(\mathfrak S_{H,c}(\mathcal{H}_1)\right)
    \cap
    \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2).
\]
Since $\mathfrak S_{H,c}(\mathcal{H}_1)$ is trace-norm closed and
$\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}$ is trace-norm continuous, the inverse image
is trace-norm closed. The state space
$\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)$ is also trace-norm closed in
$\mathcal{T}^{(1)}_S(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)$. Therefore $\mathcal C_c$ is
trace-norm closed.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:quadratic-schrodinger-esa}
Let $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ be the standard canonical vector on
\(L_2(\mathbb R^m)\) introduced in
Section~\ref{subsec:standard-ccr-representation}. Let
\(M\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)\), \(\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb R^{2m}\), and
\(c\in\mathbb R\). Define, on \(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\),
\[
\hat h^{(0)}_{M,\mathbf{b},c}
:=
\frac12\,\hat{\mathbf{R}}^\top M\hat{\mathbf{R}}
+
\mathbf{b}^\top\hat{\mathbf{R}}
+
c.
\]
Then \(\hat h^{(0)}_{M,\mathbf{b},c}\) is essentially self-adjoint on
\(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\). Moreover, if \(\mathcal{K}\) is a Hilbert space, then $\hat H^{(0)}_{M,\mathbf{b},c}
:=
\hat h^{(0)}_{M,\mathbf{b},c}\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{K}$
is essentially self-adjoint on
\(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathcal{K}
\subset L_2(\mathbb R^m)\otimes \mathcal{K}\), where $\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}$ is the algebraic tensor product.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Since \(M\) is real symmetric and \(b,c\) are real, the operator
\(\hat h^{(0)}_{M,\mathbf{b},c}\) is the Weyl quantization of a real quadratic polynomial on
phase space. Hence it is essentially self-adjoint on \(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\) by the
criterion of Fulsche--van Luijk~\cite[Thm.~1]{FulscheVanLuijk2025}. Indeed, a quadratic
polynomial has bounded derivatives of all orders at least two, so the hypotheses of that
criterion are satisfied.

Since \(\hat h^{(0)}_{M,\mathbf{b},c}\) is essentially self-adjoint
on \(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\), its closure \(\hat h_{M,\mathbf{b},c}\) is self-adjoint. Therefore
\(\hat h_{M,\mathbf{b},c}\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{K}\) is self-adjoint on \(L_2(\mathbb R^m)\otimes \mathcal{K}\), and
\(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathcal{K}\) is a core for this tensor-product
operator. Thus
\(\hat H^{(0)}_{M,\mathbf{b},c}\) is essentially self-adjoint on
\(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathcal{K}\).
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
By the Stone--von Neumann theorem with
multiplicity, there exist a Hilbert space \(\mathcal{K}\), a matrix
\(L\in\mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)\) satisfying $L^\top(\hbar\Omega_m)L=\Theta$, and a unitary $U:L_2(\mathbb R^m)\otimes \mathcal{K}\to \mathcal{H}$
such that $U^\dagger\mathbf{R}U
=
(L^\top\hat{\mathbf{R}})\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{K}$. Hence, on the domain $\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathcal{K}$, the transformed operator is
\[
U^\dagger H^{(0)}_{G,\mathbf{a},c} U
=
\left(
\frac12\,\hat{\mathbf{R}}^\top LGL^\top\hat{\mathbf{R}}
+
(L\mathbf a)^\top\hat{\mathbf{R}}
+
c\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{L_2(\mathbb R^m)}
\right)\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_\mathcal{K}.
\]
This is the operator of Lemma~\ref{lem:quadratic-schrodinger-esa} with $M=LGL^\top$ and $\mathbf{b}=L\mathbf{a}$.
Since \(G\) is real symmetric, \(M=LGL^\top\) is also real symmetric. Therefore
Lemma~\ref{lem:quadratic-schrodinger-esa} implies that the restriction of
\( U^\dagger H^{(0)}_{G,\mathbf{a},c}U\) to
\(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathcal{K}\) is essentially self-adjoint.

Finally, under the standard CCR representation with multiplicity,
\[
\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathcal{K}
\subset U^\dagger\mathcal H_R^\infty.
\]
The restriction of \(U^\dagger H^{(0)}_{G,\mathbf{a},c}U\) to
\(U^\dagger\mathcal H_R^\infty\) is therefore a symmetric extension of its
essentially self-adjoint restriction to
\(\mathscr S(\mathbb R^m)\otimes_{\mathrm{alg}}\mathcal{K}\). Since a symmetric
extension of an essentially self-adjoint operator has the same self-adjoint
closure, this extension is also essentially self-adjoint. By unitary
equivalence, \(H^{(0)}_{G,\mathbf{a},c}\) is essentially self-adjoint on
\(\mathcal H_R^\infty\).
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- deff-11: body_md -->
Let $E$ be a normed vector space with norm $\|\cdot\|$ and let $\psi:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be an extended real-valued function. Its effective domain is $\operatorname{Dom} \psi:=\{x\in E:\psi(x)<+\infty\}$. We say $\psi$ is \emph{proper} if $\operatorname{Dom} \psi\neq\emptyset$ and $\psi\not\equiv+\infty$.
<!-- end deff-11 -->
<!-- deff-12: body_md -->
Let $E$ be a normed vector space and $E^*$ denote the dual of $E$, with duality pairing $\langle f,x\rangle$ for $(f,x)\in E^*\times E$. The Legendre--Fenchel conjugate of a proper function $F:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ is the function $F^*:E^*\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ defined by
\[
F^*(f)\ :=\ \sup_{x\in E}\,\{\langle f,x\rangle - F(x)\}.
\]
<!-- end deff-12 -->
<!-- theo-2: body_md -->
\label{app:FRTheorem}
Let $E$ be a normed vector space and let $\psi,\phi:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper convex functions. Assume there exists $x_0\in \operatorname{Dom} \psi\cap \operatorname{Dom} \phi$ at which $\psi$ is continuous. Then
\[
\inf_{x\in E}\{\psi(x)+\phi(x)\}
\;=\;
\sup_{f\in E^*}\{-\psi^*(-f)-\phi^*(f)\}
\;=\;
-\min_{f\in E^*}\{\psi^*(-f)+\phi^*(f)\}.
\]
Moreover, the supremum on the dual side is attained, i.e., there exists $f^\star\in E^*$ achieving the maximum.
<!-- end theo-2 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lemma:idmnorm}
Let $\Lambda\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H})^*$ be positive semidefinite, i.e.\ $\Lambda(B)\ge0$ for all $B\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H})$ with $B\ge0$. Then $\|\Lambda\|_*=\Lambda(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}})$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lemma:b*decomposition}
Let $\Lambda\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H})^*$. There exist a unique $T\in\mathcal{T}^{(1)}_S(\mathcal{H})$ and a unique $L\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H})^*$ such that
\[
\Lambda(B)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(TB)+L(B)\quad(\forall B\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H})),\qquad L|_{\mathcal{K}_S(\mathcal{H})}=0.
\]
If moreover $\Lambda\ge0$, then $T\ge0$, $L\ge0$, $\|T\|_1\le \|\Lambda\|_*$, and $\|L\|_*\le \|\Lambda\|_*$.
In finite dimension one has $L\equiv0$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lemma:equalB*traceclass}
Let $\mathcal{H}_1,\mathcal{H}_2$ be separable Hilbert spaces and $\Lambda\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)^*$ be positive semidefinite. Assume there exist $\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1)$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_2)$ such that
\[
\Lambda(B_1\oplus B_2)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(B_1\rho)+\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(B_2\sigma)\quad\text{for all }B_1\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_1),\ B_2\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_2).
\]
Then there exists a coupling $\pi\in\Gamma(\rho,\sigma)$ such that
\[
\Lambda(B)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(B\,\pi)\quad\text{for all }B\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2).
\]
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- prop-22: body_md -->
\label{prop:B*confine}
Let $C$ be a nonnegative self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal{H}$ with compact
resolvent, and let $\Lambda\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H})^*$ be positive. By
Lemma~\ref{lemma:b*decomposition}, write
\[
\Lambda(B)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi\,B)+L(B),\quad \pi\in\mathcal{T}^{(1)}_{S}(\mathcal{H}),\ L\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H})^*,\ L\ge0,\ L|_{\mathcal{K}_S(\mathcal{H})}=0.
\]
Then
\[
\Lambda(C):=\sup\Big\{\Lambda(B):\ B\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}),\ B\le C\Big\}
=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C\,\pi), & \text{if }L\equiv0,\\[2mm]
+\infty, & \text{if }L\not\equiv0.
\end{cases}
\]
<!-- end prop-22 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
If $L\equiv0$ the supremum equals $\sup_{B\le C}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi B)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi C)$ by monotone convergence along the spectral truncations of $C$.

Assume $L\not\equiv0$. Then $\mathcal{H}$ must be infinite-dimensional.
Because $C$ has compact resolvent, it has purely discrete spectrum
$\{\lambda_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ with $\lambda_j\to+\infty$ by
Corollary~\ref{cor:cost-compact-resolvent}; let
$\{e_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ be corresponding eigenvectors. By
Lemma~\ref{lemma:idmnorm}, $L(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}})=\|L\|_*>0$. Let $P_n:=\sum_{i=1}^n |e_i\rangle\langle e_i|$; then $P_n\in\mathcal{K}_S(\mathcal{H})$ and $L(P_n)=0$, so
$L(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}-P_n)=L(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}})=\|L\|_*$ for all $n$.
Since $\lambda_i\uparrow\infty$, for any $m>0$ there exists $n(m)$ with
$C\ge m(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}-P_{n(m)})$. Hence
\[
\sup_{B\le C}\Lambda(B)\ \ge\ \Lambda\big(m(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}-P_{n(m)})\big)
= m\,\big[\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\big(\pi(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}-P_{n(m)})\big)+\|L\|_*\big]\ \geq m\|L\|_*\xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{}\ +\infty.
\]
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- prop-23: body_md -->
\label{prop:type2costoperator}
Let $\mathcal{H}_1,\mathcal{H}_2$ be separable Hilbert spaces and let
$C\in\mathcal{L}_{\geq}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)$ be a quadrature-generated
cost, with canonical generators $R_j$ on $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $S_j$ on
$\mathcal{H}_2$, $j\in[2m]$. Assume that the one-body square-sum
$H_1:=\sum_{j=1}^{2m}R_j^2$ has compact resolvent.
Let $\sigma\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_2)$, and let
$\Lambda\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2)^*$ be positive and satisfy
$\Lambda(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}\otimes B)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(B\sigma)$ for every
$B\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_2)$. Then
\[
\Lambda(C)=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(C\pi),&
\text{if }\Lambda(\cdot)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi\,\cdot)
\text{ for some }\pi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2),\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
<!-- end prop-23 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
The marginal condition gives $\Lambda(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2})=1$.
By Lemma~\ref{lemma:b*decomposition}, write
$\Lambda(B)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(TB)+L(B)$, where $T\geq0$ is trace-class,
$L\geq0$, and $L$ vanishes on compact operators.
If $L=0$, then $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(T)=1$ and the claim follows from the
normal-state evaluation of $\Lambda(C)$.

Suppose that $\delta:=L(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2})>0$.
Since the common smooth-vector space of the $S_j$ is dense,
there exists a finite-rank orthogonal projection $P$ on $\mathcal{H}_2$
whose range is contained in $\bigcap_{j=1}^{2m}\operatorname{Dom}(S_j)$ and such
that $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(P\sigma)>1-\delta/2$.
Set $\kappa_P:=\sum_{j=1}^{2m}\|S_jP\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2<\infty$.
On the common smooth core,
\[
(R_j\otimes P)\psi
=
(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}\otimes P)
(R_j\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_2}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}\otimes S_j)\psi
+
(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}\otimes PS_j)\psi.
\]
Here $PS_j$ extends to the bounded adjoint of $S_jP$.
Squaring, summing, and passing to the closed forms gives
\[
H_1\otimes P
\leq
2C+2\kappa_P\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2}.
\]
For $a>0$, let $E_a:=\mathbf1_{[0,a)}(H_1)$.
Compact resolvent makes $E_a$ finite rank, and
$H_1\geq a(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}-E_a)$. Hence the bounded self-adjoint operator
\[
B_a:=\frac a2(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}-E_a)\otimes P
-\kappa_P\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1\otimes\mathcal{H}_2}
\]
satisfies $B_a\leq C$.
Since $E_a\otimes P$ is finite rank and
$\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(T)=1-\delta$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Lambda((\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_1}-E_a)\otimes P)
&=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(P\sigma)-\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(T(E_a\otimes P))\\
&\geq\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(P\sigma)-\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(T)>\delta/2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The definition of the extended evaluation therefore yields
$\Lambda(C)\geq\Lambda(B_a)>a\delta/4-\kappa_P$.
Letting $a\rightarrow+\infty$ proves $\Lambda(C)=+\infty$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- prop-24: body_md -->
\label{prop:gAE-convex-proper}
Assume that the constrained barycentric state set defined in \eqref{eq:constrain} is nonempty, i.e.
\[
    \mathcal{S}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\mathcal{H}_0)
    :=
    \left\{
    \rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0):
    \operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_\ell\rho)\le E_\ell,\quad \ell\in[k]
    \right\}
    \neq\varnothing.
\]
Then the functional \(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}:\prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) defined in \eqref{eq:defg} is convex and proper. Moreover, $g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\boldsymbol 0)=0$.
<!-- end prop-24 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Convexity follows from the fact that \(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\) is an
infimal projection of an affine functional over a convex set of
representations. Explicitly, if \((B_s^{(0)})_{s\in[N]}\) and \((B_s^{(1)})_{s\in[N]}\) admit
representations $(B_s^{(j)})_{s\in[N]}
=
\left((\sum_{\ell=1}^k U_{s,j}^{(\ell)})\oplus V_{s,j}\right)_{s\in[N]}$ for $j=0,1$ with $-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_{s,j}^{(\ell)}
\le
\eta_{\ell,j}A_\ell$, then, for \(t\in[0,1]\), the convex combinations
\[
\widetilde U_s^{(\ell)}
=
tU_{s,0}^{(\ell)}+(1-t)U_{s,1}^{(\ell)},\quad
\widetilde V_s
=
tV_{s,0}+(1-t)V_{s,1},\quad
\widetilde\eta_\ell
=
t\eta_{\ell,0}+(1-t)\eta_{\ell,1}
\]
give an admissible representation of
\((tB^{(0)}_s+(1-t)B^{(1)}_s)_{s\in[N]}\). The corresponding objective value is the same
convex combination of the two objective values. 

It remains to show that \(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\) does not take the value
\(-\infty\). Choose $\rho_0\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\mathcal{H}_0)$. For any admissible representation $\bigl((U_s^{(\ell)})_{s\in[N],\,\ell\in[k]},
(V_s)_{s\in[N]},(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]}\bigr)$ of \(B\), we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(B_s(\rho_0\otimes\sigma_s)\right)
&=
\sum_{\ell=1}^k
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left[
\left(
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}
\right)\rho_0
\right]
+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}
\le
\eta_\ell A_\ell$ and $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_\ell\rho_0)\le E_\ell$, we obtain $-\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left[
\left(
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}
\right)\rho_0
\right]
\le
\eta_\ell E_\ell$.

Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lb}
-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
+
\sum_{\ell=1}^k\eta_\ell E_\ell
\ge
-
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(B_s(\rho_0\otimes\sigma_s)\right).
\end{equation}
The right-hand side is finite because \(B_s\) is bounded and
\(\rho_0\otimes\sigma_s\) is trace-class. Hence the infimum defining
\(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(B)\) is bounded below for every
\(B\in\operatorname{Dom}(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E})\). Thus
\(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\) never takes the value \(-\infty\).

Finally, setting $\bigl((U_s^{(\ell)})_{s\in[N],\,\ell\in[k]},
(V_s)_{s\in[N]},(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]}\bigr)$ to be all zero shows that \(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(0)\le0\). Applying the preceding
lower bound \eqref{eq:lb} with \((B_s)_{s\in[N]}=\boldsymbol{0}\) gives \(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(0)\ge0\). Hence $g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\boldsymbol 0)=0$ and \(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\) is proper.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- prop-25: body_md -->
\label{prop:FR-left-identification-constrained}
Let \(f,g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}:\prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be defined in \eqref{eq:def:f} and \eqref{eq:defg}, respectively.

Then
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:FR-left-energy-constrained}
\begin{aligned}
&\inf_{(B_s)_{s\in[N]}\in
\prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)}
\left\{
f((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
+
g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
\right\}
\\
&\qquad
=
-
\sup
\left\{
\sum_{s=1}^N \alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
-
\sum_{\ell\in[k]}\eta_\ell E_\ell
:
((U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]},(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]})
\in
\mathsf{Pot}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\right\},
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where $\mathsf{Pot}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)$ is defined in \eqref{eq:pot}.
<!-- end prop-25 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
By definition, \(f((B_s)_{s\in[N]})<+\infty\) if and only if
$B_s\le C_s$ for all $s\in[N]$, and in this case \(f((B_s)_{s\in[N]})=0\). For such \((B_s)_{s\in[N]}\), the definition of
\(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\) gives the infimum of
$-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)+\sum_{\ell=1}^k\eta_\ell E_\ell$
over all representations $B_s=
\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^k U_s^{(\ell)}\right)\oplus V_s$ with
$\eta_\ell\ge0$ and $-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}
\le
\eta_\ell A_\ell$ for all $\ell\in[k]$.

Since \(B_s\le C_s\), eliminating the auxiliary variables \(B_s\) is
equivalent to imposing directly $
\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^k U_s^{(\ell)}\right)\oplus V_s
\le C_s$ together with the same energy-potential constraints. This is precisely the
condition that $((U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]},(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]})
\in
\mathsf{Pot}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)$, where \(U_s=\sum_{\ell=1}^k U_s^{(\ell)}\).

Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\inf_{(B_s)_{s\in[N]}}
\left\{
f((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
+
g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}((B_s)_{s\in[N]})
\right\}
\\
&\quad =
\inf
\left\{
-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
+
\sum_{\ell=1}^k\eta_\ell E_\ell
:
((U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]},(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]})
\in
\mathsf{Pot}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\right\}
\\
&\quad =
-
\sup
\left\{
\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
-
\sum_{\ell=1}^k\eta_\ell E_\ell
:
((U_s,V_s)_{s\in[N]},(\eta_\ell)_{\ell\in[k]})
\in
\mathsf{Pot}_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^{\mathbf C,\boldsymbol\alpha}
(\boldsymbol\sigma)
\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:FR-left-energy-constrained}.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- prop-26: body_md -->
\label{prop:conjugate-f-cost-constraint}
Let \(f:\prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be defined in \eqref{eq:def:f}. Then, for every $\Lambda=(\Lambda_s)_{s\in[N]}\in \prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)^*$, one has the Fenchel conjugate $f^*:\prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)^*\to(-\infty,+\infty]$:
\[
f^*(\Lambda)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{s=1}^N \Lambda_s(C_s),
&
\Lambda_s\ge0\ \text{for all }s\in[N],
\\[2mm]
+\infty,
&
\text{otherwise}
\end{cases}.
\]
Here \(\Lambda_s\ge0\) means that $\Lambda_s(B)\ge0$ for all $B\in\mathcal{B}_\geq(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)$, and for a positive functional \(\Lambda_s\), its extended evaluation on the possibly unbounded cost \(C_s\) is understood as in \eqref{eq:ext-eval}.
<!-- end prop-26 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Suppose that \(\Lambda_{s_0}\) is not positive for some
\(s_0\in[N]\). Then there exists $D\in\mathcal{B}_\geq(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_{s_0})$ such that \(\Lambda_{s_0}(D)<0\). For every \(t>0\), set $B_{s_0}:=-tD$ and $B_s:=0$ for \(s\neq s_0\). Since \(C_s\ge0\), this choice satisfies \(B_s\le C_s\) for all \(s\).
Hence
\[
f^*(\Lambda)
\ge
\sum_{s=1}^N\Lambda_s(B_s)
=
-t\Lambda_{s_0}(D)\to+\infty
\quad \text{as }t\to+\infty.
\]
Thus \(f^*(\Lambda)=+\infty\).

It remains to consider the case in which every $\Lambda_s$ is
positive. By the definition of the Fenchel conjugate and the
independence of the constraints in $s$,
\[
f^*(\Lambda)
=
\sum_{s=1}^N
\sup_{\substack{B_s\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)\\ B_s\le C_s}}
\Lambda_s(B_s)
=
\sum_{s=1}^N\Lambda_s(C_s),
\]
where the last equality is precisely the extended evaluation from
\eqref{eq:ext-eval}.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- prop-27: body_md -->
\label{prop:conjugate-gAE}
Assume that \(\alpha_s>0\) for all \(s\in[N]\). Let $g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}$ be defined as in \eqref{eq:defg}. For every $\Lambda=(\Lambda_s)_{s\in[N]}
\in
\prod_{s=1}^N
\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)^*$, we have the Fenchel conjugate $g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*:\prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)^*\to(-\infty,+\infty]$:
\[
g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*(\Lambda)
=
\iota_{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bar}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}}(\Lambda)
=
\begin{cases}
0,
&
\Lambda\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bar}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E},
\\[1mm]
+\infty,
&
\text{otherwise}
\end{cases},
\]
where \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bar}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\) is defined by:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bar}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}
:=
\Bigl\{
&
\Lambda=(\Lambda_s)_{s\in[N]}
\in
\prod_{s=1}^N
\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)^*
:
\\
&
\exists\,
\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0)^*, \Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}\geq0,
\ \text{such that}
\\
&
\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(A_\ell)\le E_\ell,
\qquad \ell\in[k],
\\
&
\Lambda_s(U\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_s})
=
-\alpha_s\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(U),
\qquad
U\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0),\ s\in[N],
\\
&
\Lambda_s(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes V)
=
-\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V\sigma_s),
\qquad
V\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_s),\ s\in[N]
\Bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
<!-- end prop-27 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
By the definition of \(g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\), its Fenchel conjugate is
the supremum:
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*(\Lambda)
=
\sup
\Bigg\{
&
\sum_{\ell=1}^k\sum_{s=1}^N
\Lambda_s(U_s^{(\ell)}\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_s})
+
\sum_{s=1}^N
\left[
\Lambda_s(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes V_s)
+
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V_s\sigma_s)
\right]
-
\sum_{\ell=1}^k\eta_\ell E_\ell
\Bigg\},
\end{aligned}
\]
over all $\eta_\ell\ge0$, $V_s\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_s)$, $U_s^{(\ell)}\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0)$ such that $-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}
\le
\eta_\ell A_\ell$ for all $\ell\in[k]$.


The variables \(V_s\) are unconstrained. Therefore the supremum over
\(V_s\) is finite if and only if $\Lambda_s(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes V)=-\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V\sigma_s)$ for every $V\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_s)$ and $s\in[N]$.

Assume from now on that the above condition holds. Then the \(V_s\)-part
contributes \(0\). For the \(U_s^{(\ell)}\)-variables, fix
\(\ell\in[k]\). Taking \(\eta_\ell=0\) and restricting to variations with
$\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}=0$ shows that finiteness forces the map
\[
(U_s^{(\ell)})_{s\in[N]}
\longmapsto
\sum_{s=1}^N\Lambda_s(U_s^{(\ell)}\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_s})
\]
to vanish on this kernel. Hence there exists
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0)^*$ such that
\[
\Lambda_s(U\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_s})
=
-\alpha_s\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(U),
\qquad
U\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0),\ s\in[N],
\]
and the constraint permits
$-\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)})\leq0$ for all $\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}\ge0$, which requires $\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}\geq0$.


Under these conditions, set
$X_\ell:=-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s U_s^{(\ell)}\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0)$. Because every $\alpha_s$ is positive, every bounded self-adjoint $X_\ell$ can be realized by a choice of the $U_s^{(\ell)}$. For $\eta_\ell=0$, the supremum over $X_\ell\leq0$ is zero. For $\eta_\ell>0$, positive homogeneity of the extended evaluation in~\eqref{eq:ext-eval} gives the following expression without any $0\cdot(+\infty)$ ambiguity:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{\substack{\eta_\ell\ge0,\ X_\ell\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0)\\
X_\ell\le\eta_\ell A_\ell}}
\bigl\{\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(X_\ell)-\eta_\ell E_\ell\bigr\}
=
\max\left\{0,
\sup_{\eta_\ell>0}
\eta_\ell\bigl(\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(A_\ell)-E_\ell\bigr)
\right\}
\\
&\qquad=
\begin{cases}
0,&\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(A_\ell)\le E_\ell,\\
+\infty,&\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(A_\ell)>E_\ell.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the second case includes $\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(A_\ell)=+\infty$; thus the argument applies without assuming that $A_\ell$ is bounded.

Therefore
$g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*(\Lambda)=0$ on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bar}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\), and it is
\(+\infty\) outside this set.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- prop-28: body_md -->
\label{prop:FR-right-identification-constrained}
Let \(f,g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}:\prod_{s=1}^N \mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be defined in \eqref{eq:def:f} and \eqref{eq:defg}.

Assume that there exists $s_0\in[N]$ such that either $C_{s_0}$ has compact resolvent or $C_{s_0}$ is quadrature-generated and its associated first one-body square-sum has compact resolvent. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{\Lambda\in
\prod_{s=1}^N\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)^*}
\left\{
-f^*(-\Lambda)-g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*(\Lambda)
\right\} =
-
\inf_{(\pi_s)_s\in
\Gamma_{\mathrm{joint}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\boldsymbol\sigma)}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi_s C_s).
\end{aligned}
\]
<!-- end prop-28 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
By Propositions~\ref{prop:conjugate-f-cost-constraint} and
\ref{prop:conjugate-gAE}, the expression $-f^*(-\Lambda)-g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*(\Lambda)$ is finite only if $-\Lambda_s\ge0$ for all $s\in[N]$ and
$\Lambda\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bar}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}$. Then there exists
\(\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0)^*,\ \Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}\geq0\) such that $\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(A_\ell)\le E_\ell$ for all $\ell\in[k]$, and
\[
-\Lambda_s(U\otimes \operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_s})
=
\alpha_s\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(U),
\qquad
-\Lambda_s(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes V)
=
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V\sigma_s).
\]
Moreover, on this feasible set,
Proposition~\ref{prop:conjugate-f-cost-constraint} gives
\[
-f^*(-\Lambda)-g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*(\Lambda)
=-\sum_{s=1}^N(-\Lambda_s)(C_s),
\]
where every extended evaluation is applied to the positive functional
$-\Lambda_s$.

If the above value is finite, then
\((-\Lambda_s)(C_s)<+\infty\) for every \(s\). Set $\Xi_s:=-\alpha_s^{-1}\Lambda_s$.
Then $\Xi_s\ge0$ and, by the second marginal identity,
$\Xi_s(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\otimes V)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(V\sigma_s)$ for every
$V\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_s)$.

We use the following normality observation. Let $\Xi\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}\otimes\mathcal{K})^*$ be positive. If both marginal functionals $U\mapsto\Xi(U\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{K}})$ and $V\mapsto\Xi(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}\otimes V)$ are normal, then $\Xi$ is normal. Indeed, choose increasing finite-rank projections $P_n\uparrow\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}$ and $Q_n\uparrow\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{K}}$ such that both normal marginal tails converge to zero. Since
\[
\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}\otimes\mathcal{K}}-P_n\otimes Q_n
\leq
(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}-P_n)\otimes\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{K}}
+
\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}}\otimes(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{K}}-Q_n),
\]
one has $\Xi(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}\otimes\mathcal{K}}-P_n\otimes Q_n)\to0$. Write $\Xi(B)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(TB)+L(B)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:b*decomposition}. Because $P_n\otimes Q_n$ is finite rank, $L(P_n\otimes Q_n)=0$, and hence
\[
0\leq L(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}\otimes\mathcal{K}})
=L(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}\otimes\mathcal{K}}-P_n\otimes Q_n)
\leq\Xi(\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{\mathcal{H}\otimes\mathcal{K}}-P_n\otimes Q_n)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus $L=0$, proving the observation.

Since $\Xi_{s_0}(C_{s_0})<+\infty$, Proposition~\ref{prop:B*confine} in the compact-resolvent case and Proposition~\ref{prop:type2costoperator} in the quadrature-generated case show that $\Xi_{s_0}$ is normal. Its first marginal is $\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}$, so there exists $\rho\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0)$ such that $\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(U)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(U\rho)$ for every $U\in\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0)$. For every $s\in[N]$, the first marginal of $\Xi_s$ is therefore the normal state induced by $\rho$, while its second marginal is the normal state induced by $\sigma_s$. The normality observation gives a state $\pi_s\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)$ such that $-\Lambda_s(\cdot)=\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi_s\,\cdot)$.
The marginal identities give $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_s}\pi_s=\rho$ and $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\mathcal{H}_0}\pi_s=\sigma_s$. By~\eqref{eq:ext-eval} and Proposition~\ref{prop:spectral-trunc-positive}, the bound
\(\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(A_\ell)\le E_\ell\) is precisely
$\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_\ell\rho)\le E_\ell$ for all $\ell\in[k]$, also when $A_\ell$ is unbounded.
The same extended-evaluation identity gives $\Xi_s(C_s)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi_sC_s)$ for every $s\in[N]$.

Thus $(\pi_s)_s\in
\Gamma_{\mathrm{joint}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\boldsymbol\sigma)$, and $-\sum_{s=1}^N(-\Lambda_s)(C_s)=-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi_sC_s)$.

Conversely, if $(\pi_s)_s\in
\Gamma_{\mathrm{joint}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\boldsymbol\sigma)$ has common barycentric marginal \(\rho\), define $-\Lambda_s(\cdot):=\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi_s\,\cdot)$ and set $\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}(\cdot):=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\rho\,\cdot)$. Then $\Lambda_{\mathrm{bar}}\geq0$, \(-\Lambda_s\ge0\), \(\Lambda\in
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bar}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}\), and $-f^*(-\Lambda)-g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*(\Lambda)=-\sum_{s=1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi_sC_s)$.

Therefore the Fenchel--Rockafellar right-hand side is exactly the supremum
of the negatives of the constrained joint primal costs:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{\Lambda\in
\prod_{s=1}^N\mathcal{B}_S(\mathcal{H}_0\otimes\mathcal{H}_s)^*}
\left\{
-f^*(-\Lambda)-g_{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}^*(\Lambda)
\right\}=
-
\inf_{(\pi_s)_s\in
\Gamma_{\mathrm{joint}}^{\mathbf A,\mathbf E}(\boldsymbol\sigma)}
\sum_{s=1}^N
\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\pi_s C_s).
\end{aligned}
\]
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- prop-29: body_md -->
\label{prop:dualfunccov}
Recall $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ and $g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ defined in Section~\ref{subsubsec:faithful-covariance-dual}. Then $f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ and $g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ are proper convex functions. Moreover,
for $\mathbf Z=(Z_r)_{r\in[k]}$ with
$Z_r\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\mathrm{sa}}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$, let $(Z_r)_{ij}$ denote its
$(i,j)$-th $2m\times2m$ block. Then
\[
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cov}}^*(\mathbf Z)
=
\left(
\sum_{r=1}^k\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{11},\,
2\operatorname{Re} (Z_1)_{12},\ldots,2\operatorname{Re} (Z_k)_{12}
\right),
\]
and
\[
(f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
-\sum_{r=1}^k
\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
Z_r^\dagger
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&0\\
0&\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\end{pmatrix}
\right],
&
Z_r\preceq0,\quad r\in[k],
\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

If $\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{12}\neq-\alpha_r\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$ for some $r\in[k]$, then $(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)=+\infty$. Otherwise, when $k<N$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)
=
\sup_{\substack{
\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_m^{\mathrm Q},\\
A_s\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s),\
s=k+1,\ldots,N}}
\left\{
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\left(
\sum_{r=1}^k\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{11}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\right)\Sigma
\right]
+
2\sum_{s=k+1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)
\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
If $k=N$, then
\[
(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)
=
\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)}
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\left(
\sum_{r=1}^N\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{11}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\right)\Sigma
\right].
\]
<!-- end prop-29 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
We first verify that $f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ and $g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ are proper and convex.
For any $t>\hbar/2$, set $\mathbf V_0:=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cov}}(t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m},0,\ldots,0)$. By \eqref{eq:faithful-inputs},
\[
(\mathbf V_0)_r+
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&0\\
0&\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\end{pmatrix}
\succ0,
\quad r\in[k],
\]
so $f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ is proper and is convex by the convexity of $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$.

The domain of $g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ is nonempty, since for $t>\hbar/2$, $0\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m},\Sigma_s)$ for all $s\in[N]$. For fixed $\mathbf V$, the relation
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cov}}(\Sigma,A_1,\ldots,A_k)=\mathbf V$ fixes
$\Sigma,A_1,\ldots,A_k$. Moreover, for each $s>k$,
$\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s)$ is bounded: by the standard factorization of a positive block matrix \cite[Prop.~1.3.2]{Bhatia2007PDM}, $A_s\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s)$ if and only if there exists $K_s\in\mathcal{M}_{2m}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$ such that $\|K_s\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq1$ and 
\[ 
A_s=(\Sigma+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m)^{1/2}K_s(\Sigma_s+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m)^{1/2}. 
\]
Therefore $\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s)$ is compact since it is closed by the defining linear matrix inequality. Thus every nonempty fiber of $g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$ is compact, and the linear objective attains a finite minimum. Convexity follows directly from
the convexity of the sets
$\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s)$ in the joint variables
$(\Sigma,A_s)$ and the linearity of the objective.

For $\mathbf Z=(Z_r)_{r\in[k]}$, a direct block computation gives
\[
\operatorname{Re}\sum_{r=1}^k
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
Z_r^\dagger
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma&A_r\\
A_r^\top&0
\end{pmatrix}
\right]
=
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\left(\sum_{r=1}^k\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{11}\right)\Sigma
\right]
+
2\sum_{r=1}^k
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[(\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{12})^\top A_r\right],
\]
which proves the formula for $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{cov}}^*$.

By definition of $f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)
&=
-\sum_{r=1}^k
\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
Z_r^\dagger
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_m&0\\
0&\Sigma_r+\frac{i\tau\hbar}{2}\Omega_m
\end{pmatrix}
\right]
+
\sum_{r=1}^k
\sup_{X_r\succeq0}\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(Z_r^\dagger X_r).
\end{aligned}
\]
The last supremum is zero if $Z_r\preceq0$ for every $r\in[k]$,
since then $\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(Z_r^\dagger X_r)\leq0$ for all $X_r\succeq0$,
with equality at $X_r=0$. If $Z_r\not\preceq0$ for some $r$, choosing
$X_r=tuu^\dagger$ along a direction $u$ with $u^\dagger Z_ru>0$ and
letting $t\to\infty$ shows that the supremum is $+\infty$. This proves
the stated formula for $(f_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*$.

Finally,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)
=
\sup\quad&
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\left(
\sum_{r=1}^k\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{11}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\right)\Sigma
\right]
+
2\sum_{r=1}^k
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\bigl(\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{12}+\alpha_r\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\bigr)^\top A_r
\right]
\\
&+
2\sum_{s=k+1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s).
\end{aligned}
\]
When $k<N$, the supremum is taken over
$\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_m^{\mathrm Q}$ and
$A_s\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s)$ for $s>k$, while
$A_1,\ldots,A_k$ are unrestricted. When $k=N$, it is taken over
$\Sigma\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ and unrestricted
$A_1,\ldots,A_N$. 

Hence finiteness requires $\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{12}=-\alpha_r\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}$ for $r\in[k]$. Under these conditions, the terms involving $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ vanish. For $k<N$, this gives
\[
(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)
=
\sup_{\substack{
\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_m^{\mathrm Q},\\
A_s\in\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\Sigma,\Sigma_s),\
s=k+1,\ldots,N}}
\left\{
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\left(
\sum_{r=1}^k\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{11}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\right)\Sigma
\right]
+
2\sum_{s=k+1}^N\alpha_s\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_s)
\right\}.
\]
If $k=N$, it reduces to
\[
(g_{\mathrm{cov}}^\tau)^*(\mathbf Z)
=
\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)}
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\left[
\left(
\sum_{r=1}^N\operatorname{Re} (Z_r)_{11}-\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\right)\Sigma
\right].
\]
This proves the stated formulas.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- prop-30: body_md -->
\label{prop:unitary-realification}
Let $P^{\mathrm{shuf}}_m$ be the permutation matrix such that $(P^{\mathrm{shuf}}_m)^\top
(x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_m,y_m)^\top
=
(x_1,\ldots,x_m,y_1,\ldots,y_m)^\top$.

For $V\in U(m)$, define
\[
O_V
:=
P^{\mathrm{shuf}}_m
\begin{pmatrix}
\operatorname{Re} V&-\operatorname{Im} V\\
\operatorname{Im} V&\operatorname{Re} V
\end{pmatrix}
(P^{\mathrm{shuf}}_m)^\top.
\]
Then
$O_V\in\operatorname{Sp}(2m,\mathbb R)\cap O(2m)$, and
$V\mapsto O_V$ is a group isomorphism
\[
U(m)
\cong
\operatorname{Sp}(2m,\mathbb R)\cap O(2m).
\]
<!-- end prop-30 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:unitary-spectral-coordinates}
Let $U_0=
\frac1{\sqrt2}
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}
1&1\\
i&-i\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\mathbb U_m:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^m{}_D U_0$. With the same permutation matrix
$P^{\mathrm{shuf}}_m$ as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:unitary-realification}, one has
\[
O_{\overline V}
=
\mathbb U_mP^{\mathrm{shuf}}_m
\bigl(V\oplus_D\overline V\bigr)
(P^{\mathrm{shuf}}_m)^\top
\mathbb U_m^\dagger.
\]
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:Williamson-Gaussian-source}
Let $\hat\pi\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ have mean vector
$\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}\in\mathbb R^{4m}$ and covariance matrix
$\Sigma\in\mathrm{Cov}_{2m}^{\mathrm Q}$. Let $p$ be the number of
symplectic eigenvalues of $\Sigma$ equal to $\hbar/2$.

For every integer $q$ with $0\leq q\leq p$, there exist
$S\in\operatorname{Sp}(4m,\mathbb R)$, a Gaussian unitary $\hat U_S$
implementing $S$, and a state
$\hat\eta\in\mathcal{S}_2^R(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m-q}))$ with zero mean such that the map
$\Phi_G:\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m-q}))
\rightarrow\mathcal T^{(1)}(L_2(\mathbb R^{2m}))$ defined by
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\Phi_G(\hat\rho)
:=
&W_{\mathrm{CCR}}\!\left(
\frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}}{\hbar}
\right)
\hat U_S
\left(
|0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes q}
\otimes\hat\rho
\right)
\hat U_S^\dagger
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}\!\left(
\frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}}{\hbar}
\right)^\dagger
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:faithful-Williamson-Gaussian-channel}
\end{equation}
is a quantum channel satisfying $\hat\pi=\Phi_G(\hat\eta)$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Choose a Williamson decomposition $\Sigma=SDS^\top$ with
$D=\frac{\hbar}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2p}\oplus_D
\bigoplus_{j=p+1}^{2m}{}_D\nu_j\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2$ and $\nu_j>\hbar/2$ for $j>p$.
Let $\hat U_S$ be a Gaussian unitary implementing $S$, and define
$\hat\pi_0:=\hat U_S^\dagger
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(\frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}}{\hbar})^\dagger
\hat\pi
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(\frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}}{\hbar})
\hat U_S$.
Then $\hat\pi_0$ has zero mean and covariance $D$.

Each of its first $p$ one-mode marginals has zero mean and covariance
$(\hbar/2)\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2$, and hence is the one-mode Fock ground state
$|0\rangle\langle0|$. Since a state with a pure marginal factorizes,
there exists a state $\hat\eta_0$ on $2m-p$ modes such that
$\hat\pi_0=|0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes p}\otimes\hat\eta_0$.

For any $q\leq p$, set
$\hat\eta:=|0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes(p-q)}\otimes\hat\eta_0$.
Then $\hat\eta$ is a state on $2m-q$ modes with zero first moments,
and
\[
\hat\pi
=
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}\!\left(
\frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}}{\hbar}
\right)
\hat U_S
\left(
|0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes q}
\otimes\hat\eta
\right)
\hat U_S^\dagger
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}\!\left(
\frac{\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}}{\hbar}
\right)^\dagger.
\]
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:fock-ancilla-Gaussian-channel}
In the setting of
Lemma~\ref{lem:Williamson-Gaussian-source}, the channel $\Phi_G$ is
Gaussian. More precisely, write the column partition
$S=(S_0\ S_1)$, where
$S_0\in\mathbb R^{4m\times2q}$ and
$S_1\in\mathbb R^{4m\times2(2m-q)}$ according to the Fock-ground-state and
input modes. Then
\begin{equation}
\chi_{\Phi_G(\hat\rho)}(\boldsymbol\xi)
=
\chi_{\hat\rho}(S_1^\top\boldsymbol\xi)
\exp\left(
i\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}^\top\boldsymbol\xi
-
\frac12
\boldsymbol\xi^\top
\left(
\frac{\hbar}{2}S_0S_0^\top
\right)
\boldsymbol\xi
\right).
\label{eq:fock-ancilla-Gaussian-channel}
\end{equation}
Thus, in the notation of Definition~\ref{def:gaussian-channel},
$\mathbb X_G=S_1$,
$\mathbb Y_G=\frac{\hbar}{2}S_0S_0^\top$, and
$\mathbf m_G=\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}$.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
The Weyl transformation rule gives
\[
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}/\hbar)^\dagger
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(\boldsymbol\xi)
W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(\Omega_{2m}\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}/\hbar)
=e^{i\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}^\top\boldsymbol\xi}W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(\boldsymbol\xi).
\]
The Gaussian-unitary transformation rule gives
$\hat U_S^\dagger W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(\boldsymbol\xi)\hat U_S
=W_{\mathrm{CCR}}(S^\top\boldsymbol\xi)$.
Since
$S^\top\boldsymbol\xi
=(S_0^\top\boldsymbol\xi,S_1^\top\boldsymbol\xi)$,
the characteristic function factorizes as
\[
\chi_{\Phi_G(\hat\rho)}(\boldsymbol\xi)
=e^{i\mathbf m_{\hat\pi}^\top\boldsymbol\xi}
\chi_{|0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes q}}(S_0^\top\boldsymbol\xi)
\chi_{\hat\rho}(S_1^\top\boldsymbol\xi).
\]
The $q$-mode Fock ground state has covariance
$(\hbar/2)\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2q}$. Substituting its characteristic function in the
preceding identity gives \eqref{eq:fock-ancilla-Gaussian-channel}.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:faithful-dual-Williamson}
Let $\Sigma$ and $p$ be as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:Williamson-Gaussian-source}. Suppose that
$Z\in\mathcal{M}_{4m,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$ satisfies
$(\Sigma+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m})Z=0$.
Then $\operatorname{Re} Z\succeq0$ and
$\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Re} Z)$ is even. Writing
$q:=\frac12\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Re} Z)$, one has $q\leq p$.

The parameters in
Lemmas~\ref{lem:Williamson-Gaussian-source}
and~\ref{lem:fock-ancilla-Gaussian-channel}
can be chosen with this value of $q$ and with a symplectic matrix
$S\in\operatorname{Sp}(4m,\mathbb R)$ such that for some $d_1,\ldots,d_q>0$ and $\nu_{p+1},\ldots,\nu_{2m}>\frac{\hbar}{2},$
\[
\Sigma=SDS^\top,\quad
D=\frac{\hbar}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2p}\oplus_D
\bigoplus_{j=p+1}^{2m}{}_D\nu_j\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2,\quad
S^\top ZS
=
\bigoplus_{j=1}^q{}_D
\frac{d_j}{2}
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-i\\i&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)
\oplus_D0_{2(2m-q)},
\]
and $\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)=S\left(\{0\}^{2q}\oplus\mathbb R^{2(2m-q)}\right)$.

Writing the column partition
$S=(S_0\ S_1)$, where
$S_0\in\mathbb R^{4m\times2q}$ and
