$S_1\in\mathbb R^{4m\times2(2m-q)}$, one has
$\operatorname{Ran}(S_1)=\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)$. In particular, $S_1$ has
full column rank.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Since $Z\succeq0$ is Hermitian, $\operatorname{Re} Z\succeq0$. Let $\Sigma=S_{\mathrm W}DS_{\mathrm W}^\top$ be a Williamson
decomposition of $\Sigma$ as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:williamson}, where
$D=\frac{\hbar}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2p}\oplus_D
\bigoplus_{j=p+1}^{2m}{}_D\nu_j\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2$ and $\nu_j>\hbar/2$.
Since $S_{\mathrm W}\in\operatorname{Sp}(4m,\mathbb R)$, we have
$\Sigma+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
=S_{\mathrm W}(D+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m})S_{\mathrm W}^\top$,
so the assumed relation is equivalent to
\[
\left(
D+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)
S_{\mathrm W}^\top ZS_{\mathrm W}
=
0.
\]

Recall
$U_0=\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\i&-i\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and
$\mathbb U=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{2m}{}_D U_0$ from
Remark~\ref{rem:unitary-spectral-coordinates}. Since $U_0^\dagger
\left(
c\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_1
\right)
U_0
=
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}c-\hbar/2&0\\0&c+\hbar/2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, we have
\[
\mathbb U^\dagger
\left(
D+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
\right)
\mathbb U
=
\bigoplus_{j=1}^p{}_D
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&0\\0&\hbar\end{smallmatrix}\right)
\oplus_D
\bigoplus_{j=p+1}^{2m}{}_D
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\nu_j-\hbar/2&0\\0&\nu_j+\hbar/2\end{smallmatrix}\right).
\]

Let $P_p^{\mathrm{shuf}}$ be the permutation matrix from
Proposition~\ref{prop:unitary-realification}. We have
\[
(P_p^{\mathrm{shuf}}\oplus_D\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2(2m-p)})^\top[
\bigoplus_{j=1}^p{}_D
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&0\\0&\hbar\end{smallmatrix}\right)
\oplus_D
\bigoplus_{j=p+1}^{2m}{}_D
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\nu_j-\hbar/2&0\\0&\nu_j+\hbar/2\end{smallmatrix}\right)](P_p^{\mathrm{shuf}}\oplus_D\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2(2m-p)})=0_p\oplus_D\Xi,
\]
where $\Xi
:=
\hbar\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_p
\oplus_D
\bigoplus_{j=p+1}^{2m}{}_D
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\nu_j-\hbar/2&0\\0&\nu_j+\hbar/2\end{smallmatrix}\right)
\succ0$.


The covariance slackness condition $(\Sigma+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m})Z=0$ finally gives
\[
(0_p\oplus_D\Xi)B=0,
\]
where $B:=(P_p^{\mathrm{shuf}}\oplus_D\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2(2m-p)})^\top
\mathbb U^\dagger
S_{\mathrm W}^\top ZS_{\mathrm W}
\mathbb U
(P_p^{\mathrm{shuf}}\oplus_D\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2(2m-p)})\succeq0$. Consequently,
$\operatorname{Ran} B\subseteq\ker(0_p\oplus_D\Xi)
=\operatorname{\mathbb{C}}^p\oplus\{0\}^{4m-p}$. Since $B$ is Hermitian, there exists
$M_Z\in\mathcal{M}_{p,\geq}(\operatorname{\mathbb{C}})$ such that
$B=M_Z\oplus_D0_{4m-p}$.

Let $r=\operatorname{rank} M_Z\leq p$, and choose $V\in U(p)$ such that
\[
V^\dagger M_ZV
=
\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_r,0,\ldots,0),
\quad
d_1,\ldots,d_r>0.
\]
By Remark~\ref{rem:unitary-spectral-coordinates}, let $O_{\overline{V}}$ be the orthogonal symplectic matrix corresponding to $\overline{V}$. $O_{\overline V}\oplus_D\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2(2m-p)}
\in\operatorname{Sp}(4m,\mathbb R)\cap O(4m)$ and preserves $D$. Hence
$S:=S_{\mathrm W}(O_{\overline V}\oplus_D\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2(2m-p)})$
gives $\Sigma=SDS^\top$ and $\Sigma+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m}
=S(D+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\Omega_{2m})S^\top$, and
\[
S^\top ZS
=
\bigoplus_{j=1}^r{}_D
U_0
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_j&0\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)
U_0^\dagger
\oplus_D0_{2(2m-r)}
=
\bigoplus_{j=1}^r{}_D
\frac{d_j}{2}
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-i\\i&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)
\oplus_D0_{2(2m-r)}.
\]
The last equality is obtained by $U_0\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d&0\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)U_0^\dagger
=\frac d2\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-i\\i&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Moreover,
\[
S^\top(\operatorname{Re} Z)S
=
\frac12
\operatorname{diag}
\left(
d_1\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2,\ldots,d_r\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2,
0_{2(2m-r)}
\right).
\]
Therefore $r=\frac12\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{Re} Z)=q$, and
$\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)=S\left(\{0\}^{2q}\oplus\mathbb R^{2(2m-q)}\right)$ follows.
Since $\Sigma=SDS^\top$ with the same $D$ as above and $q\leq p$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:Williamson-Gaussian-source} applies with this $q$
and this $S$. Writing $S=(S_0\ S_1)$ gives
$\operatorname{Ran}(S_1)=\ker(\operatorname{Re} Z)$. Since $S$ is invertible, $S_1$ has full
column rank.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- prop-31: body_md -->
\label{prop:covidm}
Let $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, $\Sigma_{\rho},\Sigma_{\sigma}
\in\mathcal{M}_{2,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb{R})$ and $X\in\mathcal{M}_2(\mathbb{R})$. If
\[
M_\tau:=
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma_{\rho} & X\\
X^{\top} & \Sigma_{\sigma}
\end{pmatrix}
+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega\oplus_D(\tau\omega)\bigr)
\succeq0,
\]
then
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_{\rho}}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\\[1mm]
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_{\sigma}}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\end{pmatrix}
+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega\oplus_D(\tau\omega)\bigr)
\succeq0.
\]
<!-- end prop-31 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Consider the Pauli matrices
\[
P_1=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&1\\
1&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
P_2=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&-i\\
i&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
P_3=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&0\\
0&-1
\end{pmatrix},\qquad 
P_4=\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2.
\]
Then $P_j\omega P_j
=(-1)^j\omega$ and $
\frac14\sum_{j=1}^4P_j AP_j
=
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} A}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2$ for all $A\in\mathcal{M}_2(\mathbb R)$. Therefore, for $j\in[4]$,
\[
(P_j\oplus_D P_j) M_{\tau}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
P_j\Sigma_{\rho}P_j
&
P_j XP_j
\\
(P_j XP_j)^{\top}
&
P_j\Sigma_{\sigma}P_j
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i(-1)^j\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega\oplus_D(\tau\omega)\bigr).
\]
Since each $P_j\oplus_D P_j$ is unitary and Hermitian, and since both unitary congruence and transposition preserve positive semidefiniteness, we have
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
&\frac14\left[\left(\sum_{j=1,3}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)^\dagger M_{\tau}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)\right)^\top+\sum_{j=2,4}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)^\dagger M_{\tau}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)\right]\\
=&\frac14\left[\left(\sum_{j=1,3}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)M_{\tau}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)\right)^\top+\sum_{j=2,4}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)M_{\tau}(P_j\oplus_D P_j)\right]\\
=&\begin{pmatrix}
\frac14\sum_{j=1}^4P_j\Sigma_{\rho}P_j
&
\frac14\sum_{j=1}^4P_j XP_j
\\
\frac14\sum_{j=1}^4(P_j XP_j)^{\top}
&
\frac14\sum_{j=1}^4P_j\Sigma_{\sigma}P_j
\end{pmatrix}+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega\oplus_D(\tau\omega)\bigr)\\
=&\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_{\rho}}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\\[1mm]
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_{\sigma}}{2}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega\oplus_D(\tau\omega)\bigr)
\succeq0.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
The resulting matrix is positive semidefinite, since it is an average of positive semidefinite matrices and their transposes.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- coro-6: body_md -->
\label{coro:multimode-isotropic-reduction}
Let $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, $\Sigma_\rho,\Sigma_\sigma
\in\mathcal{M}_{2m,\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$,
and $X\in\mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)$. If
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma_\rho & X\\
X^{\top} & \Sigma_\sigma
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}
\bigl(\Omega_m\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_m)\bigr)
\succeq0,
\]
then
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_\rho}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\\[1mm]
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_\sigma}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}
\bigl(\Omega_m\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_m)\bigr)
\succeq0.
\]
<!-- end coro-6 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
For \(j\in[m]\), let $\Sigma_{\rho}^{(j)}$, $X^{(j)}$, and $
\Sigma_{\sigma}^{(j)}$ denote the $2\times2$ diagonal blocks corresponding to rows and columns $2j-1$ and $2j$ of $\Sigma_{\rho}$, $X$, and $
\Sigma_{\sigma}$, respectively. Since principal compressions preserve positive semidefiniteness and $\Omega_m=\bigoplus_{j=1}^m{}_D\omega$, we obtain
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma_{\rho}^{(j)} & X^{(j)}\\
(X^{(j)})^{\top} & \Sigma^{(j)}_{\sigma}
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}
\bigl(\omega\oplus_D(\tau\omega)\bigr)
\succeq0.
\]
Applying the one-mode result, Proposition~\ref{prop:covidm}, gives
\[
M_j:=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_{\rho}^{(j)}}2\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X^{(j)}}2\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\\[1mm]
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X^{(j)}}2\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_{\sigma}^{(j)}}2\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}
\bigl(\omega\oplus_D(\tau\omega)\bigr)
\succeq0.
\]
Averaging over all modes yields
\[
\overline M
:=
\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m M_j
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_\rho}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\\[1mm]
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_\sigma}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}
\bigl(\omega\oplus_D(\tau\omega)\bigr)
\succeq0,
\]
where we used $\sum_{j=1}^m\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_{\rho}^{(j)}=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_\rho$, $\sum_{j=1}^m\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X^{(j)}=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X$ and $
\sum_{j=1}^m\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_{\sigma}^{(j)}=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_\sigma$. Therefore, the positive semidefiniteness is preserved for the Kronecker product $\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_m\otimes\overline M\succeq0$. After permuting the coordinates from the mode-wise ordering to the subsystem-wise ordering, we obtain
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_\rho}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\\[1mm]
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}} X}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
&
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\Sigma_\sigma}{2m}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\end{pmatrix}
+
\frac{i\hbar}{2}
\bigl(\Omega_m\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_m)\bigr)
\succeq0.
\]
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
We prove the formula for the quantum-state formulation. The formula for the quantum-channel formulation
follows from \cite[Thm.~3]{DPaTre19}, after restoring $\hbar$ and using
the cost normalization in \eqref{eq:tau-cost}.

By Theorem~\ref{thm:Gaussian-opt-plan}, we may restrict to Gaussian optimal couplings.
For a Gaussian optimal plan $\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}}^{G}\mapsto(\hat\rho^{\rm th},\hat\sigma^{\rm th})$, its mean is $(\mathbf{m}_{\hat{\rho}},\mathbf{m}_{\hat{\sigma}})$ by Proposition \ref{prop:reduction-moments}. We write its covariance as
\[
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}}^{G}}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
w_{\hat\rho}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m} & A\\
A^\top & w_{\hat\sigma}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Sigma_{\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}}^{G}}+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\,(\Omega_m\oplus_D\Omega_m)\succeq0,
\]
with $A\in\mathcal{M}_{2m}(\mathbb R)$. By Corollary~\ref{coro:multimode-isotropic-reduction}, feasibility of the above implies feasibility of
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
w_{\hat\rho}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m} & \frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A)}{2m}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\\[2pt]
\frac{\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A)}{2m}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m} & w_{\hat\sigma}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\end{pmatrix}
+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\,(\Omega_m\oplus_D\Omega_m)\succeq0.
\]
Let $\hat\pi_{\mathrm{iso}}^{G}$ be the Gaussian state with the same bipartite mean and this block
covariance. Since the cost depends only on first and second moments by Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC}, we have $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\hat C^{(+1)}\,\hat\pi_{\mathrm{iso}}^{G})
=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\hat C^{(+1)}\,\hat\pi_{\mathrm{opt}}^{G})$. Hence we may restrict to the one-parameter family
\[
\left\{
\begin{pmatrix}
w_{\hat\rho}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m} & c\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\\[2pt]
c\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m} & w_{\hat\sigma}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\end{pmatrix}
\ :\ c\in\mathbb R,\ 
\begin{pmatrix}
w_{\hat\rho}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m} & c\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}\\
c\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m} & w_{\hat\sigma}\,\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_{2m}
\end{pmatrix}
+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\,(\Omega_m\oplus_D\Omega_m)\succeq0
\right\}.
\]

Using the decomposition and
$\Omega_m=\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_m\otimes\omega$,
the RS constraint splits into $m$ identical $4\times4$ blocks; positivity is equivalent to
\[
M(c):=
\begin{pmatrix}
w_{\hat\rho} & \tfrac{i\hbar}{2} & c & 0\\
-\tfrac{i\hbar}{2} & w_{\hat\rho} & 0 & c\\
c & 0 & w_{\hat\sigma} & \tfrac{i\hbar}{2}\\
0 & c & -\tfrac{i\hbar}{2} & w_{\hat\sigma}
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
The eigenvalues of $M(c)$ are
\[
\lambda_{1,2}=-\frac{\hbar}{2}+\frac{w_{\hat\rho}+w_{\hat\sigma}}{2}
\pm \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(w_{\hat\rho}-w_{\hat\sigma})^{2}+4c^{2}},
\quad
\lambda_{3,4}=\frac{\hbar}{2}+\frac{w_{\hat\rho}+w_{\hat\sigma}}{2}
\pm \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(w_{\hat\rho}-w_{\hat\sigma})^{2}+4c^{2}}.
\]
Thus $M(c)\succeq0$ iff $\lambda_{\min}(M(c))\ge0$, i.e.
\[
\sqrt{(w_{\hat\rho}-w_{\hat\sigma})^{2}+4c^{2}}
\le w_{\hat\rho}+w_{\hat\sigma}-\hbar,
\]
which yields the maximal feasible $c_{\max}
=\sqrt{\Big(w_{\hat\rho}-\frac{\hbar}{2}\Big)\Big(w_{\hat\sigma}-\frac{\hbar}{2}\Big)}$.

By Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC}, we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,+1}^2(\hat\rho^{\rm th},\hat\sigma^{\rm th})
={}&\|\mathbf{m}_{\hat\rho}-\mathbf{m}_{\hat\sigma}\|^2+\min_{c\ \text{feasible}}\ 2m\,(w_{\hat\rho}+w_{\hat\sigma}-2c)
\\
={}&\|\mathbf{m}_{\hat\rho}-\mathbf{m}_{\hat\sigma}\|^2+2m\Big(w_{\hat\rho}+w_{\hat\sigma}-2c_{\max}\Big).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substituting $c_{\max}$ and completing the square gives
\[
\operatorname{\mathcal{QW}}_{2,+1}^2(\hat\rho^{\rm th},\hat\sigma^{\rm th})
=2m\Big(\sqrt{w_{\hat\rho}-\tfrac{\hbar}{2}}
-\sqrt{w_{\hat\sigma}-\tfrac{\hbar}{2}}\Big)^{2}+\|\mathbf{m}_{\hat\rho}-\mathbf{m}_{\hat\sigma}\|^2+2m\hbar,
\]
as claimed.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:nonfaithful-boundary-couplings}
For the states in Example~\ref{ex:nonfaithful-boundary}, every
$\hat\rho_t^\tau$, with $t\in[-1,1]$ and
$\tau\in\{\pm1\}$, is an equal-weight $2$-QW barycenter of
$\hat\sigma_1$ and $\hat\sigma_2$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:tensorization-barycenter},
$\hat\rho_0^{+1}=\left(\hat\sigma_{3\hbar/4}^{\mathrm{th}}\right)^{\otimes2}$ and
$\hat\rho_0^{-1}=\left(\hat\sigma_{\hbar}^{\mathrm{th}}\right)^{\otimes2}$ are barycenters
for $\tau=+1$ and $\tau=-1$, respectively, and therefore determine the
corresponding minimum barycenter values.

For $\tau=+1$, set
$A_{1,t}^{+}=\frac{\hbar}{2}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&0\\ t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and
$A_{2,t}^{+}=\frac{\hbar}{2}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2\\ 0&\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$.
For $\tau=-1$, set
$A_{1,t}^{-}=\hbar\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&0\\ t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and
$A_{2,t}^{-}=\hbar\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&t\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2\\ 0&\operatorname{\mathbb{I}}_2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. For every $s\in\{1,2\}$ and $|t|\leq1$, direct substitution gives $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\overline\Sigma_t^\tau&A_{s,t}^\tau\\
(A_{s,t}^\tau)^\top&\Sigma_s\end{smallmatrix}\right)
+\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\Omega_2\oplus_D(\tau\Omega_2)\bigr)\succeq0$. Thus $A_{s,t}^\tau\in
\mathrm{Corr}_\tau(\overline\Sigma_t^\tau,\Sigma_s)$. Let
$\hat\pi_{s,t}^\tau\in\Gamma_\tau(\hat\rho_t^\tau,\hat\sigma_s)$
be the centered Gaussian coupling with covariance
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\overline\Sigma_t^\tau&A_{s,t}^\tau\\
(A_{s,t}^\tau)^\top&\Sigma_s\end{smallmatrix}\right)$.

Since $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(\overline\Sigma_t^\tau)$ and $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}(A_{s,t}^\tau)$ are
independent of $t$, Proposition~\ref{prop:stateTrC} gives $\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(\hat C^{(\tau)}\hat\pi_{s,t}^\tau\right)=\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(\hat C^{(\tau)}\hat\pi_{s,0}^\tau\right)$. At $t=0$, $\hat\rho_0^\tau$ is the tensor-product barycenter above,
and $\hat\pi_{s,0}^\tau$ is the tensor product of the corresponding one-mode optimal couplings. Hence $\frac12\sum_{s=1}^2
\operatorname{\mathrm{Tr}}\!\left(\hat C^{(\tau)}\hat\pi_{s,t}^\tau\right)
=
B_\tau(\hat{\boldsymbol{\sigma}}\mid\boldsymbol{\alpha})$. Therefore $\hat\rho_t^\tau$ attains the minimum and is an equal-weight
$2$-QW barycenter of $\hat\sigma_1$ and $\hat\sigma_2$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
